display_title: [XLA] Redirect only aliasing uses when copying shared read only values

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Redirect only aliasing uses when copying shared read only values

When `CopyRemover` elides one of several copies of a constant or unaliased
entry parameter, that read only value joins a buffer with other values.
`CopyInsertion::AddSpecialCaseCopies` previously inserted a fresh copy and
replaced every use of the read only instruction. That rewrite turned every
other surviving copy into a double copy chain and routed pure read only
consumers through the new copy, extending its live range.

Trace backward from every site where a read only value shares a buffer (while
carries, conditional branch roots, in place operations, `Pin`, view colored
outputs, and aliased entry roots) to collect the exact operand edges and root
positions that need a writable buffer. Redirect only those consumers to the
copy, splitting shared `kGetTupleElement` and `kBitcast` chains when needed and
preserving control dependencies and active schedules. Remaining copies and pure
readers continue to read the immutable value directly while leaving it in a
singleton `HloBuffer`. Copies requested by `custom_buffer_analysis` or
disallowed operand sharing still replace all uses.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:copy_insertion_test`: verifies shared constants, read
  only array and tuple entry parameters, shared bitcasts, controlled tuple
  elements, views, custom buffer callbacks, and scheduled modules.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026463116

head_commit.message:
Fix 32-bit overflow in SPMD pad-with-wrap rotation amount

In `SpmdPartitioner::PreprocessHlos` (`xla/service/spmd/spmd_partitioner.cc`),
widen `rotate_lhs_amount` from `int` to `int64_t` (matching `rotate_rhs_amount`

rotation amounts exceeding `INT32_MAX` do not truncate or overflow. Also guard
the `padded_size > INT32_MAX` pad-with-wrap rewrite on matching even shardings
for `mid` and `hlo` and bounded halo size (`low_pad + high_pad <=
min(INT32_MAX, shard_size)`) so uneven sharding or large halos fall back to
standard `kConcatenate` partitioning instead of hitting 32-bit halo helpers.

display_title: [XLA] Hoist loop invariant layout changing copies in LICM

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Hoist loop invariant layout changing copies in LICM

When `WhileLoopInvariantCodeMotion` runs after layout assignment and fusion
with `hoist_reshapes` enabled and `hoist_other` disabled, it skips every opcode
other than `kConstant` and `kReshape`. That leaves unfused layout changing
`kCopy` instructions and decomposed `kBitcast` to `kCopy` or `kReshape` chains
executing inside the loop body on every iteration.

Allow `WhileLoopInvariantCodeMotion` to hoist layout changing array `kCopy`
instructions in the default memory space under `hoist_reshapes`. Also trace
through default memory space `kBitcast` operands that feed a hoisted copy or
reshape. Same layout buffer isolation copies and copies or bitcasts in any
nondefault memory space are never hoisted. Standalone bitcasts without a
hoisted user remain in the loop body and add no tuple state. The size inflation
check evaluates in double precision over layout aware shape sizes and rejects
copies that expand padded storage.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:while_loop_invariant_code_motion_test` pins layout copy
  and bitcast chain hoisting, attribute preservation, `CopyInsertion`, same
  layout and nondefault memory space rejection, and size inflation limits.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Make symmetric memory consumers aware of the window offset.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Make symmetric memory consumers aware of the window offset.

`CollectiveMemory::FindWeakSymmetricMemory` now returns the byte offset of the allocation inside the symmetric window instead of always 0. `CollectiveKernelThunk` remembers that offset next to the cached window and rebuilds its peer pointer table when it changes. The ragged all-to-all bounds check validates writes against both the destination buffer slice and the symmetric window.

Today every window is registered for exactly one allocation, so the offset is always 0 and behavior does not change. This prepares for registering one window for a whole collective memory arena, where buffers live at non-zero offsets inside the window.

display_title: PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

head_commit.message:
PR #52971: [AlgebraicSimplifier] Gate constant reciprocal division rewrite on fast math

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52971

#ai-generated

Fixes #52968.

## Status quo

`HandleDivide` rewrites floating-point division by a constant into multiplication by a rounded reciprocal, including when `enable_fast_math` is false.

## Why

We encountered this while comparing an ONNX quantized MLP across execution backends. For float32 `[-100, 0.1, 100]`, the scale `200 / 255` changes by one ULP. The subsequent zero-point calculation crosses a rounding boundary, producing 127 instead of 128. The issue includes an independent JAX reproduction with CPU fast math disabled.

## Design choices

Require `enable_fast_math` for this rewrite. Add scalar and broadcasted-constant tests with fast math disabled, and explicitly enable fast math in the existing reciprocal-rewrite tests.

In `xla/service/cpu/tests/onednn_matmul_test.cc`, enable CPU fast math in `DivisionByConstantWithEltwiseLinearF32` (since oneDNN `LINEAR` post-op fusion relies on `AlgebraicSimplifier` rewriting constant division to multiplication) and add `DivisionByConstantWithoutFastMathNotFusedF32` to verify that division remains unfused when fast math is disabled.

## Trade-offs

This retains the rewrite in fast-math mode. With fast math disabled, it preserves division and may reduce strength-reduction opportunities. Performance impact has not been benchmarked.

## Testing

All tests in `//xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test` pass.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Release cached symmetric memory when collective buffers are freed.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Release cached symmetric memory when collective buffers are freed.

The PJRT GPU client now adds a sub-allocator free visitor that calls `gpu::ReleaseSymmetricMemory`, next to the existing allocator memory registration visitors, and passes the free visitors to every collective memory allocator: the separate collective BFC allocator (through a new `CreateCollectiveBFCAllocator` parameter) and the "platform" `StreamExecutorMemoryAllocator`, in addition to the BFC and VMM allocators that already received them.

This makes sure a symmetric memory registration cached on a communicator never outlives the device allocation it was registered for. Until registrations are actually cached on communicators the visitor finds nothing to release. One cost is that the "platform" allocator now synchronizes the device before freeing a collective buffer, because it has a free visitor; a later change only installs the visitor when caching on communicators is enabled.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026430041

display_title: [jax-buildcop] [XLA:GPU] Fix out-of-bounds scatter indices read in single-block launches.

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] [XLA:GPU] Fix out-of-bounds scatter indices read in single-block launches.

In `EmitNaiveImplementation` (`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/scatter.cc`),
`thread_id_to_update_id_map` was constructed using `updates_map.GetDimVars()`.
Because `updates_map.Simplify()` absorbs single-dimension element-count
constraints into `dim_vars_` (for example tightening `th_x` from `[0, 63]` to
`[0, 41]` in a single-block launch with 42 update elements), passing those
tightened bounds into `ApplyIndexing` before the bounds check caused range
analysis to fold `index_id_in_bounds` (`slice_id < num_slices`) to constant
`true`. Inactive threads then bypassed the `scf.if` guard and read past the end
of the scatter indices buffer, causing intermittent `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`
failures when the buffer abutted an unmapped page boundary.

Construct `thread_id_to_update_id_map` using the full kernel launch grid bounds
from `launch_dimensions()` instead, and add a lit regression test verifying that
the `arith.cmpi ult` and `scf.if` guard are preserved.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026418524

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Return NaN from f32 exp when the NaN input is known at compile time

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Return NaN from f32 exp when the NaN input is known at compile time

GenerateVF32Exp froze FPToSI(n) for a NaN n. The frozen value is arbitrary,
and it reaches rem_bits, which is added to the bits of z, so exp of a
compile-time NaN could return a finite value, 0 or an infinity. Map a NaN n
to 0 before the conversion instead.

Fixes #53092

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

`KernelThunk`, `ExecuteKernelOnStream`, `KernelThunkToString`, and
`FfiLaunchParams` still handled `se::ClusterDim` separately from
`LaunchDimensions`, while `CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()` dropped
`custom_kernel_.cluster_dims()`.

Read CTA cluster dimensions directly from `LaunchDimensions::cluster_dims()`
across GPU runtime thunks and stream launch helpers, and preserve them in
`CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()`.

To preserve 2-week forward compatibility, `KernelThunk::ToProto()` dual-writes
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` alongside `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims`.
For 6-month backward compatibility, `KernelThunk::FromProto()` falls back to
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` when `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims` is
unset.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cap small-input loop unrolling at a single thread block.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cap small-input loop unrolling at a single thread block.

When `unroll_small_inputs` is enabled in `ComputeLoopFusionConfig`, small loop fusions previously unrolled up to `MaxUnrollFactor` even after fitting inside a single GPU thread block. Unrolling beyond one block leaves threads idle and inflates vector register pressure in multi-phase fusions.

Bound `max_unroll` for small inputs by `absl::bit_ceil(num_blocks)` from `CalculateLaunchDimensions`, and skip unrolling when `num_blocks` is already 1.

sibling consumer operands, the producer, and producer operands by raw pointer.
When a `dynamic-update-slice` updated `bitcast(x)` and its producer read `x`,
or the reverse, fusion added a second parameter for the same buffer. Alias
analysis then rejected in place sharing, so `CopyInsertion` inserted full
buffer copies.

Resolve operands in `xla/hlo/transforms/instruction_fusion.cc` through
`bitcast`, `tuple`, and `get-tuple-element` chains while honoring tuple shape
indices. Forbid producers that introduce a second aliasing parameter or slice a
bitcast view with a different base buffer or rank. Also peel root wrappers and
output tuples when fusing into the in place operand itself. Fusions where the
slice and update share the exact same operand, shape, and start indices remain
allowed.

Computations that previously fused reads across a bitcast into an in place
update now keep the read separate and avoid buffer copies.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:instruction_fusion_test` pins bitcast and tuple alias
  rejection, loop copy elimination, rank mismatch handling, and matching slice
  fusion.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

This is another one that _could_ be considered a candidate for ShapeTracker, which I am working on in parallel (see chain of cls after cl/1022689285). However, having a use case might make it easier to find bugs when I do this and this is only 177 lines.

Slices are tracked alongside the ShapeTracker as per-dimension ranges of the port of the dot: the ShapeTracker describes the unsliced tensor, and the ranges become the `slices` of the cuDNN tensor. Nested slices are combined.

A slice can be followed by shape transformations before it reaches the dot, e.g. `dot(transpose(slice(p)), ...)`. When a slice is reached, it is moved to the port side of the ShapeTracker (next to the dot): the steps of the ShapeTracker are replayed on the shape of the operand of the slice, carrying the sliced range of every dimension along.

Limitations:
- for merged dimensions, only the major-most dimension of a group can be sliced (otherwise you can't represent them as one stride, one range per dimension),
- for split dimensions, the range has to be aligned to the dimensions that it is split into,
- slices cannot be strided,
- slices can be in the prologue, but not epilogue (cudnn fails to execute epilogue slices with CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM_NULL_POINTER)

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cap small-input loop unrolling at a single thread block.

When `unroll_small_inputs` is enabled in `ComputeLoopFusionConfig`, small loop fusions previously unrolled up to `MaxUnrollFactor` even after fitting inside a single GPU thread block. Unrolling beyond one block leaves threads idle and inflates vector register pressure in multi-phase fusions.

Bound `max_unroll` for small inputs by `absl::bit_ceil(num_blocks)` from `CalculateLaunchDimensions`, and skip unrolling when `num_blocks` is already 1.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fold identity dynamic-update-slice of slice from same source

`AlgebraicSimplifier` did not simplify a `dynamic-update-slice` that writes an
unmodified `slice` or `dynamic-slice` of its base operand back to the same
indices. Such updates act as noops but survive into buffer assignment and force
unnecessary copies and fusions.

Fold `dynamic-update-slice(x, slice(x, starts, limits, 1), starts)` and
`dynamic-update-slice(x, dynamic-slice(x, starts, sizes), starts)` directly to
`x` in `HandleDynamicUpdateSlice`. Both `dynamic-slice` and
`dynamic-update-slice` clamp each start index to the same range, so dynamic
offsets fold with exact bit equality. Also look through `reshape` and `bitcast`
operations that only insert or delete size 1 dimensions while preserving
physical element order and tiling. Guard against dynamic shapes, buffer shapes,
layout or sharding mismatches, and control predecessors via
`ReplaceInstructionIfCompatible`. Existing program outputs are unchanged.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test` pins static
  slice, dynamic slice, degenerate size 1 reshape and bitcast folds, and
  rejection of strided, shifted, transposing, retiling, and layout mismatching
  updates.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over non-last dimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over non-last dimensions.

A Triton scan fusion processes the whole scan dimension inside each block, so its output tile sizes have no entry for that dimension. `TritonFusion::GetLaunchConfig` matched the tile sizes with the leading dimensions of the fusion root, which gives the right number of blocks only when the scan dimension is last. `CanTritonHandleScan` therefore rejected all other scans.

Skip the scan dimensions when counting tiles, and remove the check from `CanTritonHandleScan`. The scan dimensions are found by walking from the fusion roots through get-tuple-element and elementwise ops, as `TilingSpace` does.

`ScanRewriterTriton` still only rewrites scans over the minor-most dimension of the layout, so only scans over a dimension that is minor-most but not last are newly rewritten.

display_title: PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. If a split fails with an uncertain outcome, the parent keeps the child-handle storage alive until it is torn down. `PollUntilDone` now reports a failed `ncclCommGetAsyncError` query separately from an async operation error.

🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

  Added regression tests:

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- NcclErrorsTest.ReportsQueryFailureWithUnderlyingError and NcclErrorsTest.DistinguishesAsyncOperationErrorFromQueryFailure: query failures and async errors are reported differently.
- NcclTypesTest.AbortPendingSplits: null-handle handling, cleanup, and retention after an abort failure, using a fake abort (no GPU needed).

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.
Copybara import of the project:

--
0f0db98cf5ee8fc388ea04487118a4142972e8b3 by Jane Liu <janeliu@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, ncclCommSplit can return before the
child handle is published. XLA read the output immediately, so it could
see a NULL child, and NCCL could later write to a stack variable that no
longer existed.

Add NcclCommunicator::Split(), which keeps the output on the heap and
polls the parent with ncclCommGetAsyncError until the split completes
before returning the child. If the wait fails or the child is
unexpectedly NULL, the output storage is leaked with a warning, since
NCCL may still write to it. Reclaiming it after parent teardown is left
for a follow-up.

display_title: Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

head_commit.message:
Extract target-neutral LowerTensors helpers and GPU patterns

`LowerTensorsPass` currently mixes shared tensor-to-LLVM lowering with GPU
dialect ops, device capabilities, and vendor-specific atomics in one target.
As a result, XLA:CPU either pulls in GPU dependencies or relies on earlier
passes to load GPU dialects. Separate the target-neutral core from the GPU
patterns to prepare for dedicated CPU and GPU tensor-lowering passes.

Move the shared two-phase driver and tensor/atomic patterns into a
target-neutral `lower_tensors_common` library (`LowerTensors` and
`LowerTensorsConfig`) with no GPU dependencies. Trace pass-through destination
buffers via `mlir::DestinationStyleOpInterface` on `xla` and `xla_gpu` ops, and
mark `xla_gpu.allocate_shared` with `MemAlloc`.

Move GPU-specific patterns (`allocate_shared`, `sync_threads`, sub-byte
mid-word `set_dynamic_dim_size`, and NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel direct atomics)
into `LowerGpuTensors` under `xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/transforms/`.
Pre-lower `allocate_shared` before the main tensor patterns so buffer alignment
derives directly from `llvm.mlir.global`. Keep `LowerTensorsPass` as a thin
wrapper and restrict `xla_gpu` checks in `lower_tensors.mlir` to `CHECK-GPU`.

display_title: [jax-buildcop] [XLA:GPU] Fix out-of-bounds scatter indices read in single-block launches.

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] [XLA:GPU] Fix out-of-bounds scatter indices read in single-block launches.

In `EmitNaiveImplementation` (`xla/backends/gpu/codegen/emitters/scatter.cc`),
`thread_id_to_update_id_map` was constructed using `updates_map.GetDimVars()`.
Because `updates_map.Simplify()` absorbs single-dimension element-count
constraints into `dim_vars_` (for example tightening `th_x` from `[0, 63]` to
`[0, 41]` in a single-block launch with 42 update elements), passing those
tightened bounds into `ApplyIndexing` before the bounds check caused range
analysis to fold `index_id_in_bounds` (`slice_id < num_slices`) to constant
`true`. Inactive threads then bypassed the `scf.if` guard and read past the end
of the scatter indices buffer, causing intermittent `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`
failures when the buffer abutted an unmapped page boundary.

Construct `thread_id_to_update_id_map` using the full kernel launch grid bounds
from `launch_dimensions()` instead, and add a lit regression test verifying that
the `arith.cmpi ult` and `scf.if` guard are preserved.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Track explicit setting of xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 in DebugOptions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Track explicit setting of xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 in DebugOptions.

**Status quo**: `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` unconditionally sets `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` to `false`, which sets the proto3 `optional bool` presence bit on every newly constructed `DebugOptions` instance. As a result, serialized `HloModuleProtoWithConfig` modules cannot distinguish between a user who explicitly passed `--xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` in `XLA_FLAGS` / CLI flags and a user who left the flag untouched.

**Why**: Before flipping `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` to `true`, we need an indicator in serialized `DebugOptions` that records when `--xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` was explicitly passed via flags, without waiting for every binary in the fleet to rebuild.

**Design choices**: Add `optional bool xla_gpu_unsupported_explicit_bf16_default = 589;` to `DebugOptions` in `xla.proto` without setting it in `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`. Set it to `true` inside the custom setter callback for `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` in `MakeDebugOptionsFlags()`.

**Compromises**: Adds an internal tracking field to `DebugOptions` solely for rollout telemetry.

**Alternatives**: Removing `set_xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32(false)` from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` and relying on field presence alone requires every binary in the fleet to rebuild before old binaries stop emitting `false` for untouched flags.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Cap small-input loop unrolling at a single thread block.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Cap small-input loop unrolling at a single thread block.

When `unroll_small_inputs` is enabled in `ComputeLoopFusionConfig`, small loop fusions previously unrolled up to `MaxUnrollFactor` even after fitting inside a single GPU thread block. Unrolling beyond one block leaves threads idle and inflates vector register pressure in multi-phase fusions.

Bound `max_unroll` for small inputs by `absl::bit_ceil(num_blocks)` from `CalculateLaunchDimensions`, and skip unrolling when `num_blocks` is already 1.

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

- NcclErrorsTest.ReportsQueryFailureWithUnderlyingError and NcclErrorsTest.DistinguishesAsyncOperationErrorFromQueryFailure: query failures and async errors are reported differently.
- NcclTypesTest.AbortPendingSplits: null-handle handling, cleanup, and retention after an abort failure, using a fake abort (no GPU needed).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

head_commit.message:
Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

The heap simulator only lets an instruction reuse the buffer of an operand value if it consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. Reusing it also through instructions that forward the value (e.g. `get-tuple-element`, `bitcast`, `opt-barrier`, `call`) lowers the peak memory, but can add more fragmentation than it saves.

`BufferAssigner` now calls the new `HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse`. It simulates with and without this kind of reuse and keeps it only if the heap is smaller. Algorithms with a slow `Finish()` drop it without comparing if it does not lower the peak memory. The comparison is per heap simulation, so the fallback chain can stop at an earlier algorithm than before. Other callers of `HeapSimulator::Run` do not change.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022733837

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Release cached symmetric memory when collective buffers are freed.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Release cached symmetric memory when collective buffers are freed.

The PJRT GPU client now adds a sub-allocator free visitor that calls `gpu::ReleaseSymmetricMemory`, next to the existing allocator memory registration visitors, and passes the free visitors to every collective memory allocator: the separate collective BFC allocator (through a new `CreateCollectiveBFCAllocator` parameter) and the "platform" `StreamExecutorMemoryAllocator`, in addition to the BFC and VMM allocators that already received them.

This makes sure a symmetric memory registration cached on a communicator never outlives the device allocation it was registered for. Until registrations are actually cached on communicators the visitor finds nothing to release. One cost is that the "platform" allocator now synchronizes the device before freeing a collective buffer, because it has a free visitor; a later change only installs the visitor when caching on communicators is enabled.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Commit only required JIT pages and honor thread stack size on Windows

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Commit only required JIT pages and honor thread stack size on Windows

`ContiguousSectionMemoryManager` maps one block per compiled kernel object and
previously padded each section by a full page even when sections were empty or
aligned at or below page size. On Windows,
`llvm::sys::Memory::allocateMappedMemory` commits full 64 KiB allocation
granularity blocks via `VirtualAlloc(MEM_RESERVE | MEM_COMMIT)`, inflating
pagefile commit charge for small JIT kernels by up to 16x. Windows `tsl::Env`
also ignored `ThreadOptions::stack_size` and failed to record detached thread
names.

* Reserve Windows JIT blocks with `MEM_RESERVE` (`PAGE_NOACCESS`) and commit
  only the required 4 KiB pages.
* Reserve alignment padding only above `page_size` for nonempty sections and
  skip `protectMappedMemory` on empty sections.
* Use `_beginthreadex` with `STACK_SIZE_PARAM_IS_A_RESERVATION` in Windows
  `tsl::Env` and register thread names inside the thread entry function.

Tests:
- `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:page_committed_memory_test`: verifies 4 KiB page
  commit inside 64 KiB Windows reservations, subsection protection and code
  execution, and commit charge savings.
- `//xla/backends/cpu/codegen:contiguous_section_memory_manager_test`: verifies
  single page code allocations, empty reservations, and high alignment bounds.
- `//xla/tsl/platform:env_test`: verifies thread stack sizes above 1 MiB and
  thread name lookup.

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix buffer sharing and control edge handling in copy removal

Region analysis in `CopyRemover` compared same instruction definitions and uses
without calling `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser`, allowing
`RemoveUnnecessaryCopies` to drop copies protecting out of place ops aliased to
donated parameters and forcing `AddSpecialCaseCopies` to insert wide lifetime or
entry hoisted parameter copies. It also recorded forced control edges on copies
about to be removed, stripped control dependencies on subsequently elided
copies, and overwrote earlier definitions when deduplicating region entries.

* Check `CanShareOperandBufferWithUser` and post substitution sharing hazards
  (constants, multi user `sort`, and repeated operands) before eliding a copy.
* Redirect forced control edges off the candidate copy and relay nonredundant
  control dependencies across elided copies in `RemoveUnnecessaryCopies`.
* Retain all value definitions when deduplicating region entries at the same
  instruction.
* Add `HloReachabilityMap::AddReachabilityEdges` and propagate bulk reachability
  updates through `tmp_worklist_` without allocating per node hash sets.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:copy_insertion_test`: verifies donated out of place
  copies, substitution hazards, control edge redirection and relay, and merged
  definition interception.
- `//xla/hlo/analysis:hlo_reachability_test`: verifies transitive propagation in
  `AddReachabilityEdges`.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Support slices in CuDnnGemmDimensions.

This is another one that _could_ be considered a candidate for ShapeTracker, which I am working on in parallel (see chain of cls after cl/1022689285). However, having a use case might make it easier to find bugs when I do this and this is only 177 lines.

Slices are tracked alongside the ShapeTracker as per-dimension ranges of the port of the dot: the ShapeTracker describes the unsliced tensor, and the ranges become the `slices` of the cuDNN tensor. Nested slices are combined.

A slice can be followed by shape transformations before it reaches the dot, e.g. `dot(transpose(slice(p)), ...)`. When a slice is reached, it is moved to the port side of the ShapeTracker (next to the dot): the steps of the ShapeTracker are replayed on the shape of the operand of the slice, carrying the sliced range of every dimension along.

Limitations:
- for merged dimensions, only the major-most dimension of a group can be sliced (otherwise you can't represent them as one stride, one range per dimension),
- for split dimensions, the range has to be aligned to the dimensions that it is split into,
- slices cannot be strided,
- slices can be in the prologue, but not epilogue (cudnn fails to execute epilogue slices with CUDNN_STATUS_BAD_PARAM_NULL_POINTER)

[PJRT] Speed up small-dimension deinterleave with Highway.

Vectorize the deinterleave kernels for K = 2, 3, and 4 (1- to 8-byte elements)
using Highway, and enable K = 4 deinterleave (previously left on the general 2D

`transpose_kernels.cc`. Moves the kernel unit tests into

loops, negative strides, and unaligned buffers, and adds short-row benchmarks.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching rank and non-overflowing upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched ranks and allowed `origin[i] + shape.dims()[i]` to exceed `INT64_MAX`, forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand rank checks while leaving `origin[i] + shape[i]` upper-bound calculations vulnerable to signed `int64_t` overflow. In addition, `IndexDomain(Shape shape)` passed both `Index::Zeros(shape.dims().size())` and `std::move(shape)` in the same delegating constructor call, relying on unspecified C++ argument evaluation order.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and non-overflowing `origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]` upper bounds, delegate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `IndexDomain::FromProto` to `IndexDomain::Create`, initialize `origin_` and `shape_` directly in `IndexDomain(Shape shape)`, and route `operator+=` / `operator-=` through `operator+` / `operator-` so offset mutations preserve upper-bound validity.

head_commit.message:
PR #53379: [XLA:GPU] Enable portable large VMM regression coverage

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53379

#ai-generated

The allocator regression added for the [WSL VMM fix](https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52820) was disabled and required 6.5 GiB of free GPU memory. Enable it by default across CUDA platforms, requesting POSIX-FD exportability where supported and checking that backing allocations retain it.

Reduce the allocator request to 4 GiB + 1 byte and NCCL buffers to 4 GiB while retaining boundary checks. Explain why POSIX-FD exportability, distinct per-GiB patterns, and boundary readbacks matter to regression coverage.

Validation: focused CUDA allocator suite passed (9 passed, 3 hardware/version skips; RDMA-enabled cases excluded). The large-allocation test also passed with POSIX-FD support forced off. Formatting, target DWYU, and all 50 general DWYU tests passed. Native Windows and a two-GPU NCCL run were not validated locally.

The free-memory check remains a snapshot; concurrent GPU allocations can still cause resource contention.
Copybara import of the project:

--
f2d17a70e7601135750f767ef408baba1eb6cba8 by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Refine large-allocation regression tests

Skip the manual allocator regression before CUDA initialization when the
kernel is not WSL. Retain its memory guard and document isolated execution.

Explain how distinct per-GiB patterns and boundary samples check the NCCL
transfer while registration and transfer cover the entire buffer.

Validation: CUDA/NCCL builds and formatting pass. Eight allocator tests,
the isolated 6 GiB regression, and the non-WSL/unreadable-release skip
checks pass. Three locality-domain tests skip for hardware/version
requirements. NCCL execution skips because the host has one GPU.

--
2a4f95469f66980d68821f626533e335e46ba8ef by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Reduce large-allocation regression memory

Reduce the allocator regression to 4 GiB plus one byte, preserving the
short final backing chunk. Reduce the NCCL buffer to 4 GiB per GPU and
adjust the availability messages and comments.

The reduced allocator regression naturally fails with CUDA out of memory
when the chunk retry is disabled and passes with it restored. CUDA/NCCL
builds, formatting, and eight allocator tests pass. Three locality-domain
tests skip for hardware/version requirements; NCCL execution skips on the
one-GPU host.

--
52f4ddd03ed7ece7b10dbcb3deecf0d76e180fd4 by Frederic Bastien <fbastien@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:GPU] Enable the large VMM regression across CUDA platforms

Run the 4 GiB + 1 byte allocator regression in the default suite without
a WSL kernel check. Request and verify POSIX-FD handles when the device
supports them, and exercise non-exportable VMM allocations otherwise.
Retain full-buffer initialization, boundary/tail checks, and the existing
free-memory requirement. Explain the WSL origin and generic coverage.

The capability attribute is available since CUDA 10.2, below the supported
CUDA runtime and build-header floors; both queried API symbols are already
registered.

Validation: CUDA build, clang-format, DWYU, and all 50 general checks pass.
The default allocator suite passes nine tests with three hardware/version
skips. The large test also passes with POSIX-FD support overridden to zero,
with no live handles, mappings, or reservations remaining. RDMA-enabled
cases were excluded. Native Windows execution was not available locally.

Merging this change closes #53379

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over non-last dimensions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Allow Triton scans over non-last dimensions.

A Triton scan fusion loops over the scan dimension inside each block, so its output tile sizes have no entry for that dimension. `TritonFusion::GetLaunchConfig` matched the tile sizes with the leading dimensions of the fusion root, which gives the right number of blocks only when the scan dimension is last. `CanTritonHandleScan` therefore rejected all other scans.

Skip the scan dimensions when counting tiles, and remove the check from `CanTritonHandleScan`. The scan dimensions are found by walking from the fusion roots through get-tuple-element and elementwise ops, as `TilingSpace` does.

`ScanRewriterTriton` still only rewrites scans over the minor-most dimension of the layout, so only scans over a dimension that is minor-most but not last are newly rewritten.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Track explicit setting of xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 in DebugOptions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Track explicit setting of xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 in DebugOptions.

**Status quo**: `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` unconditionally sets `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` to `false`, which sets the proto3 `optional bool` presence bit on every newly constructed `DebugOptions` instance. As a result, serialized `HloModuleProtoWithConfig` modules cannot distinguish between a user who explicitly passed `--xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` in `XLA_FLAGS` / CLI flags and a user who left the flag untouched.

**Why**: Before flipping `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` to `true`, we need an indicator in serialized `DebugOptions` that records when `--xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` was explicitly passed via flags, without waiting for every binary in the fleet to rebuild.

**Design choices**: Add `optional bool xla_gpu_unsupported_explicit_bf16_default = 589;` to `DebugOptions` in `xla.proto` without setting it in `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`. Set it to `true` inside the custom setter callback for `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` in `MakeDebugOptionsFlags()`.

**Compromises**: Adds an internal tracking field to `DebugOptions` solely for rollout telemetry.

**Alternatives**: Removing `set_xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32(false)` from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` and relying on field presence alone requires every binary in the fleet to rebuild before old binaries stop emitting `false` for untouched flags.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1013032110

display_title: PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

head_commit.message:
PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. If a split fails with an uncertain outcome, the parent keeps the child-handle storage alive until it is torn down. `PollUntilDone` now reports a failed `ncclCommGetAsyncError` query separately from an async operation error.

🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:

  Added regression tests:

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- NcclErrorsTest.ReportsQueryFailureWithUnderlyingError and NcclErrorsTest.DistinguishesAsyncOperationErrorFromQueryFailure: query failures and async errors are reported differently.
- NcclTypesTest.AbortPendingSplits: null-handle handling, cleanup, and retention after an abort failure, using a fake abort (no GPU needed).

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.

--

display_title: Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

head_commit.message:
Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

The heap simulator only lets an instruction reuse the buffer of an operand value if it consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. Reusing the buffer also through other positions (instructions that forward the value, e.g. `get-tuple-element`, `bitcast`, `opt-barrier` or a `call`) lowers the peak memory, but can add more fragmentation than it saves, because the buffer stays at the same offset for longer.

`BufferAssigner` now calls the new `HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse`. It simulates with this kind of reuse and, if a buffer was reused that way, again without it. The reuse is only kept if the heap is smaller. Algorithms with a slow `Finish()` (new `HeapAlgorithm::HasFastFinish()`) drop the reuse without comparing if it does not lower the peak memory. The comparison is per heap simulation, so the fallback chain can still stop at an earlier algorithm than before.

Other callers of `HeapSimulator::Run` do not change, because the new option `may_reuse_operand_buffers_through_other_positions` is off by default.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add clique-level release of cached symmetric memory.

When a collective memory buffer is freed, any symmetric memory registration cached on a communicator for that buffer must be dropped, otherwise a later allocation at the same address would reuse a stale window.

Cliques are tracked for this in a separate registry, keyed by local device and with its own mutex, because the release will run on allocator free paths and must not wait for the process clique mutex, which can be held for a whole run while a clique is abandoned.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that the product of non-zero dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Enforce the same `Shape::kMaxNumElements` bound in `IfrtArrayType::verify`, `VifrtArrayV1Type::verify`, and `PjRtExecutable` shape conversions, remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

PR #52451: [XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52451

📝 Summary of Changes

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, `ncclCommSplit` returns before the child communicator exists. XLA used the NULL child handle right away, and NCCL could later write to a variable that no longer existed.

This adds `NcclCommunicator::Split()`, which waits on the parent until the split finishes and only then returns the child. 🎯 Justification

Recoverable JAX jobs that use nonblocking communicators and communicator splitting can fail, and later crash, when XLA uses an uninitialized child.

🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

N/A.

- GpuCollectivesTest.SplitCommunicatorsNonblocking: a nonblocking split returns valid, healthy communicators.
- NcclErrorsTest.ReportsQueryFailureWithUnderlyingError and NcclErrorsTest.DistinguishesAsyncOperationErrorFromQueryFailure: query failures and async errors are reported differently.
- NcclTypesTest.AbortPendingSplits: null-handle handling, cleanup, and retention after an abort failure, using a fake abort (no GPU needed).

🧪 Execution Tests:

N/A in XLA.

display_title: PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

head_commit.message:
PR #52875: [XLA:CPU] Prevent unsafe buffer reuse in oneDNN fusions

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52875

A fused FP32 matmul followed by `maximum(product, zeros)` can return negative values on the oneDNN/ACL path. XLA permits the output to reuse the zero operand's buffer, but matmul overwrites those zeros before maximum reads them. The regression returns `[[6, -6], [-12, 12]]` without the fix instead of `[[6, 0], [0, 12]]`.

Use a shared CPU alias policy during copy insertion, scheduling, buffer assignment and AOT loading. Custom fusions deny inferred input/output reuse by default; YNNPACK retains the usual HLO shape/use checks. oneDNN's compiled partition requirements are unavailable during compilation. Fusion remains enabled, with potentially higher buffer memory use and protective copies for aliased inputs. Saved executable formats and existing allocations are unchanged.

Validation:

- 39 focused test executions pass across AArch64 QEMU N1, SVE256 and SVE512: allocation rules, internal and aliased zero inputs, YNNPACK reuse, and AOT export/load.
- Removing only the copy-insertion policy makes both new aliased-input regressions fail while the original internal-broadcast regression still passes.
- The original 17x23 by 23x19 reproducer passes six numerical comparisons across those profiles, still using `gemm:acl` with the fused maximum.
- Clang-format 17.0.6, buildifier 6.4.0 and whitespace checks pass.

A previous broader sweep found an unrelated SVE512 batched-matmul mismatch using oneDNN's `brg:sve_512`. It predates this change and remains unresolved. These are correctness tests under emulation, not native performance measurements.

[XLA:GPU] Fix NULL child communicator after nonblocking NCCL split

With nonblocking NCCL communicators, ncclCommSplit can return before the

head_commit.message:
[ROCm profiler] Add rocm_tracer_options_utils

Second of three changes to support ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration
in the ROCm tracer. Adds the parser; nothing calls it yet.

UpdateRocmTracerOptionsFromProfilerOptions applies the gpu_* keys over
the caller's defaults and returns every problem as an error or warning,
instead of stopping at the first one as CUPTI does.
AppendOptionDiagnostics writes them to XSpace.errors/warnings and the
log.

- Event and annotation limits: a negative value is an error. For the two
  event limits, 0 means no limit, as on CUDA; passed through, it would
  empty the trace. gpu_max_annotation_strings = 0 retains none, as on
  CUDA, and draws a warning. gpu_max_activity_api_events is stored but
  not enforced yet, because the collector only counts HIP_API activity
  events; a warning says so.
- gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task: 0 or more than the device count
  means every GPU, as on CUDA. A negative value is an error. A smaller
  value draws a warning that every GPU is still traced.
- Keys CUPTI implements but ROCm does not draw a "not implemented"
  warning, whatever their value.
- Unknown gpu_* keys are errors. Other keys belong to other profiler
  components and are ignored.

RocmTraceCollectorImpl counts events in uint64_t guarded by
event_maps_mutex_, which every access already holds, instead of
std::atomic<int>, so a limit above INT_MAX no longer wraps the counter.

EveryCuptiKeyIsRecognized keeps the two key lists in sync: it reads the
CUPTI parser's source and fails if ROCm neither applies nor warns about
one of its keys. The RocmTraceCollectorOptions comments drop "if -1, no
limit".

Tests: rocm_tracer_options_utils_test, 25 host-only cases.

head_commit.message:
PR #48502: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR2)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48502

This is the second among three PRs.

We add a parser for the `gpu_*` keys in `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration`. Nothing calls it yet; #48503 wires it into GpuTracer.

The CUPTI parser stops at the first bad key and fails `Start()`. `ProfilerController` then never calls `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace and the reason is only in the log. This one applies every valid key and returns the problems as errors and warnings; `AppendOptionDiagnostics` writes them to `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and the log.

What each key does on ROCm:

- `gpu_max_callback_api_events`, `gpu_max_annotation_strings`: applied. A negative value is an error; anything above 1e9 is clamped with a warning. Callback events = 0 means "no limit" on CUDA, so here it becomes 1e9 with a warning (passed through, 0 would drop the whole trace). Annotation strings = 0 is applied and warns that kernels will have no op names.
- `gpu_max_activity_api_events`: stored, but always warns that it isn't enforced. The collector only counts HIP_API activity events, and every activity record is HIP_OPS.
- `gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task`: 0 or more than the GPU count means all GPUs, as on CUDA. Negative is an error. A smaller K is applied with a warning: all GPUs are still traced, and afterwards only K consecutive device ids are kept, starting at the lowest one that recorded an event.
- The CUPTI-only keys (NVTX, aggregated tracing, graph trace, PM sampling) and `gpu_dump_graph_node_mapping`: type-checked, then a "no effect on ROCm" warning. No warning when the value is what ROCm does anyway, e.g. `gpu_enable_nvtx_tracking=true`.
- Any other `gpu_*` key is an error. Keys without the `gpu_` prefix are left alone, since other profiler components read the same map.

Two smaller changes. The ROCm key list is a hand copy of CUPTI's, so `cupti_tracer_options_utils.cc` gets a comment (no code change), and `EveryCuptiKeyIsRecognized` reads that file and fails if a CUPTI key is missing here. The 1e9 cap is now `kMaxRocmTraceEvents` in `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, shared with `--xla_gpu_rocm_max_trace_events`, with a `static_assert` that it fits the collector's `int` counters.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests:

`rocm_tracer_options_utils_test` adds 30 host-only cases (no GPU needed). At `f8eeb882cf` on MI355X with `--config=rocm_ci_hermetic` (TheRock 10.0.0), it passes, and so do `rocm_tracer_utils_test`, `rocm_tracer_test` and `rocm_collector_test`.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

`KernelThunk`, `ExecuteKernelOnStream`, `KernelThunkToString`, and
`FfiLaunchParams` still handled `se::ClusterDim` separately from
`LaunchDimensions`, while `CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()` dropped
`custom_kernel_.cluster_dims()`.

Read CTA cluster dimensions directly from `LaunchDimensions::cluster_dims()`
across GPU runtime thunks and stream launch helpers, and preserve them in
`CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()`.

To preserve 2-week forward compatibility, `KernelThunk::ToProto()` dual-writes
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` alongside `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims`.
For 6-month backward compatibility, `KernelThunk::FromProto()` falls back to
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` when `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims` is
unset.

head_commit.message:
PR #53494: [XLA:GPU] Treat an unknown BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto kind as no algorithm

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/53494

📝 Summary of Changes

`BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm::FromProto` returns `std::nullopt` (no exact algorithm) instead of `InvalidArgument` when the `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` holds no algorithm kind this build knows: none is set, or the writer used a oneof case added after this build. The thunk emitter and `CublasLtMatmulThunk::FromProto` then fall back to the heuristic algorithm index, or fail at execution under `xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm`, exactly as they already do when no descriptor is present.

🎯 Justification

The descriptor is persisted in autotune results and serialized executables, so it must stay forward compatible. A oneof case added by a newer XLA parses into the unknown fields of an older reader, which sees `ALGORITHM_NOT_SET`. Today that is an error, so any new algorithm kind would make older runtimes fail to compile from those autotune results or to load those executables. Treating an unknown kind as "no algorithm" lets an older reader degrade to the heuristic choice, and lets a new kind ship without a default-off emission flag or staged rollout; the existing require-exact flag still decides when an exact algorithm is mandatory. A follow-up (ROCm/xla#1500) adds such a kind to record exact hipBLASLt solutions.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

🐛 Bug Fix

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `blas_lt_matmul_algorithm_test`: an unset and an unknown (unknown-field) algorithm kind both yield `std::nullopt`.
- `cuda_blas_lt_test`: updated for the `std::optional` return.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Canonicalize float TOTAL comparisons with normalized zeros and NaNs to WEAK

head_commit.message:
Canonicalize float TOTAL comparisons with normalized zeros and NaNs to WEAK

Frontends such as JAX emit floating-point total-order comparisons (for example
in `lax.sort` comparators) where both operands already canonicalize `-0.0` and
`+0.0` to the same zero bit pattern and `NaN`s to the same positive `NaN` bit
pattern. Keeping `order=TOTAL` forces `ComparisonExpander` to lower the compare
into integer bit-manipulation sequences. We try to match this expanded pattern
later on, but that does not work reliably, because e.g. `bitcast-convert` could
have been replaced by a `bitcast`. Instead of trying to account for a modified
pattern, we should use the new `order=WEAK` attribute that prevents these
issues.

Add `ComparisonCanonicalizer` to rewrite scalar
`compare(canon(lhs), canon(rhs), dir, TOTAL)` instructions in `sort` comparator
computations into `compare(lhs, rhs, dir, WEAK)` for floating-point types with
signed zero, register it in `hlo-opt`, and schedule it before `SortRewriter`
and `ComparisonExpander` in the CPU and GPU HLO pipelines.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Track explicit setting of xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 in DebugOptions.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Track explicit setting of xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32 in DebugOptions.

**Status quo**: `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` unconditionally sets `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` to `false`, which sets the proto3 `optional bool` presence bit on every newly constructed `DebugOptions` instance. As a result, serialized `HloModuleProtoWithConfig` modules cannot distinguish between a user who explicitly passed `--xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` in `XLA_FLAGS` / CLI flags and a user who left the flag untouched.

**Why**: Before flipping `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` to `true`, we need an indicator in serialized `DebugOptions` that records when `--xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` was explicitly passed via flags, without waiting for every binary in the fleet to rebuild.

**Design choices**: Add `optional bool xla_gpu_unsupported_explicit_bf16_default = 589;` to `DebugOptions` in `xla.proto` without setting it in `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()`. Set it to `true` inside the custom setter callback for `xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32` in `MakeDebugOptionsFlags()`.

**Compromises**: Adds an internal tracking field to `DebugOptions` solely for rollout telemetry.

**Alternatives**: Removing `set_xla_gpu_default_to_alg_dot_bf16_bf16_f32(false)` from `DefaultDebugOptionsIgnoringFlags()` and relying on field presence alone requires every binary in the fleet to rebuild before old binaries stop emitting `false` for untouched flags.

display_title: PR #48502: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR2)

head_commit.message:
PR #48502: [ROCm] Add ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration into the ROCm tracer (PR2)

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/48502

This is the second among three PRs.

We add a parser for the `gpu_*` keys in `ProfileOptions.advanced_configuration`. Nothing calls it yet; #48503 wires it into GpuTracer.

The CUPTI parser stops at the first bad key and fails `Start()`. `ProfilerController` then never calls `CollectData()`, so the user loses the GPU trace and the reason is only in the log. This one applies every valid key and returns the problems as errors and warnings; `AppendOptionDiagnostics` writes them to `XSpace.errors`/`warnings` and the log.

What each key does on ROCm:

- `gpu_max_callback_api_events`, `gpu_max_annotation_strings`: applied. A negative value is an error; anything above 1e9 is clamped with a warning. Callback events = 0 means "no limit" on CUDA, so here it becomes 1e9 with a warning (passed through, 0 would drop the whole trace). Annotation strings = 0 is applied and warns that kernels will have no op names.
- `gpu_max_activity_api_events`: stored, but always warns that it isn't enforced. The collector only counts HIP_API activity events, and every activity record is HIP_OPS.
- `gpu_num_chips_to_profile_per_task`: 0 or more than the GPU count means all GPUs, as on CUDA. Negative is an error. A smaller K is applied with a warning: all GPUs are still traced, and afterwards only K consecutive device ids are kept, starting at the lowest one that recorded an event.
- The CUPTI-only keys (NVTX, aggregated tracing, graph trace, PM sampling) and `gpu_dump_graph_node_mapping`: type-checked, then a "no effect on ROCm" warning. No warning when the value is what ROCm does anyway, e.g. `gpu_enable_nvtx_tracking=true`.
- Any other `gpu_*` key is an error. Keys without the `gpu_` prefix are left alone, since other profiler components read the same map.

Two smaller changes. The ROCm key list is a hand copy of CUPTI's, so `cupti_tracer_options_utils.cc` gets a comment (no code change), and `EveryCuptiKeyIsRecognized` reads that file and fails if a CUPTI key is missing here. The 1e9 cap is now `kMaxRocmTraceEvents` in `rocm_tracer_utils.h`, shared with `--xla_gpu_rocm_max_trace_events`, with a `static_assert` that it fits the collector's `int` counters.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature

🧪 Unit Tests:

`rocm_tracer_options_utils_test` adds 30 host-only cases (no GPU needed). At `f8eeb882cf` on MI355X with `--config=rocm_ci_hermetic` (TheRock 10.0.0), it passes, and so do `rocm_tracer_utils_test`, `rocm_tracer_test` and `rocm_collector_test`.

the caller's defaults and returns every problem as an error or warning,
instead of stopping at the first one as CUPTI does.
AppendOptionDiagnostics writes them to XSpace.errors/warnings and the

- Event and annotation limits: a negative value is an error. For the two
  event limits, 0 means no limit, as on CUDA; passed through, it would

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

head_commit.message:
Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

The heap simulator only lets an instruction reuse the buffer of an operand value if it consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. Reusing the buffer also through other positions (instructions that forward the value, e.g. `get-tuple-element`, `bitcast`, `opt-barrier` or a `call`) lowers the peak memory, but can add more fragmentation than it saves, because the buffer stays at the same offset for longer.

`BufferAssigner` now calls the new `HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse`. It simulates with this kind of reuse and, if a buffer was reused that way, again without it. The reuse is only kept if the heap is smaller. Algorithms with a slow `Finish()` (new `HeapAlgorithm::HasFastFinish()`) drop the reuse without comparing if it does not lower the peak memory. The comparison is per heap simulation, so the fallback chain can still stop at an earlier algorithm than before.

Other callers of `HeapSimulator::Run` do not change, because the new option `may_reuse_operand_buffers_through_other_positions` is off by default.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1022733837

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Use LaunchDimensions for CTA cluster dimensions in GPU runtime

`KernelThunk`, `ExecuteKernelOnStream`, `KernelThunkToString`, and
`FfiLaunchParams` still handled `se::ClusterDim` separately from
`LaunchDimensions`, while `CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()` dropped
`custom_kernel_.cluster_dims()`.

Read CTA cluster dimensions directly from `LaunchDimensions::cluster_dims()`
across GPU runtime thunks and stream launch helpers, and preserve them in
`CustomKernelThunk::launch_dimensions()`.

To preserve 2-week forward compatibility, `KernelThunk::ToProto()` dual-writes
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` alongside `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims`.
For 6-month backward compatibility, `KernelThunk::FromProto()` falls back to
`KernelThunkProto.cluster_dim` when `LaunchDimensionsProto.cluster_dims` is
unset.

display_title: [XLA:GPU] Add clique-level release of cached symmetric memory.

head_commit.message:
[XLA:GPU] Add clique-level release of cached symmetric memory.

Adds `ReleaseSymmetricMemory(device_id, addr)` to `GpuClique`, `LockableGpuClique` and a process-wide `gpu::ReleaseSymmetricMemory` in `gpu_cliques.h`. It forwards the release to every communicator of every live clique that runs on the given local device.

When a collective memory buffer is freed, any symmetric memory registration cached on a communicator for that buffer must be dropped, otherwise a later allocation at the same address would reuse a stale window. The allocator does not know which cliques use the buffer, so the release goes to all cliques on the device. Cliques are tracked for this in a separate registry of weak pointers with its own mutex, because the release will run on allocator free paths and must not wait for the process clique mutex, which can be held for a whole run while a clique is abandoned. No callers yet.

display_title: PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

head_commit.message:
PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52240

:pencil: **Summary of Changes**

Preserve frontend attributes when dot rewriters replace a dot with new instructions. New dots are added with `HloInstruction::AddInstruction` on the original dot, which derives them via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (also carrying metadata and, where shapes allow, sharding, like existing rewriters such as `DotDimensionSorter`), so they inherit the original dot's frontend attributes instead of silently dropping them. This covers `DotAlgorithmRewriter` (the BF16/TF32 decompositions in `backends/gpu/transforms` and the FP8xN decomposition in `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter.cc`), `ScaledDotRewriter`, `SplitkRewriter`, and `GemmFusionSwapOperands`.

:dart: **Justification**

Frontend attributes are the mechanism by which the frontend (e.g. JAX) attaches annotations to HLO instructions for downstream passes to consume. When a pass replaces an instruction, it must carry those attributes over to the replacement; otherwise the annotation is silently dropped and the consumers that depend on it no longer see it. These dot rewriters were not doing this, so annotated matmuls lost their scheduling annotations.

:compass: **Design: deriving replacements from the original dot**

Each new dot is added with `original_dot->AddInstruction(...)`, which derives it via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (metadata, frontend attributes, and sharding where the shapes allow). Instructions built by helpers call `SetupDerivedInstruction` directly: the instruction that replaces the dot in `RewriteDotWithOperandPairs` (shared by BF16X3/X6/X9 and TF32X3) and `RewriteFp8xNDot` (FP8X3/X4), and the split-K dot, which `MakeDotHlo` creates. So every new dot and the instruction that replaces the original keep the annotation.

:rocket: **Kind of Contribution**

:bug: Bug Fix

:test_tube: **Unit Tests:**

Added hardware-independent tests asserting frontend attributes survive each dot rewrite:

* `backends/gpu/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `KeepsFrontendAttributes`, parameterized over every `PrecisionConfig::Algorithm`: verifies that after the pass every dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep the attributes. Without the fix it fails for the seven algorithms the pass decomposes (BF16, BF16X3/X6/X9, TF32X3, FP8X3/X4); new algorithms are covered automatically.
* `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewriteFp8xNDotStructureTest.KeepsFrontendAttributes`, for FP8X3 and FP8X4 at both precisions: verifies every F8 dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep them.
* `gemm_fusion_swap_operands_test.cc`:
  * `SwappedDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the swapped dot keeps them.
* `scaled_dot_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewrittenDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the dot replacing a scaled-dot keeps them.
* `splitk_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `SplitKDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the split-K dot keeps them.

:test_tube: **Execution Tests:**

No new checked-in execution test was added.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Guard grouped conv output reshard fallback and divisibility

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Guard grouped conv output reshard fallback and divisibility

In `PartitionDot`, when `PartitionConv` returned `nullptr` for an unsupported
grouped convolution whose spatial windows were classified as dot dimensions, the
`conv_spatial_dims.empty()` fallback called `ReshardLHSRHSToMatchOutputSharding`
using `ParseConvolutionDimsInfo`, which ignores `feature_group_count` and
`batch_group_count`. That path sliced `rhs` output channels while keeping the
full group count, pairing channels with the wrong input groups. Separately,
`PartitionConvOnBatchOrFeatureGroupedDims` checked group divisibility only
against `lhs` shards, omitting `output_sharding` on `output_feature_dimension`
and allowing `batch_group_count` below `input_batch` on its equal dimension
shortcut, which misaligned or zeroed padded groups. Skip
`ReshardLHSRHSToMatchOutputSharding` for grouped convolutions so `PartitionDot`
falls back to replication, and require group divisibility across output feature
shards in `PartitionConvOnBatchOrFeatureGroupedDims`, with no flag.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

`PjRtCpuExecutable` currently hashes `HloModule::ToString()` for its executable fingerprint and returns early before computing a fingerprint when a module has zero parameters. Default HLO printing includes `OpMetadata`, where `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds` renumbers stack frame IDs in computation order during proto deserialization. When optimization passes introduce callee subcomputations that serialize before `ENTRY`, a deserialized executable gets a different fingerprint than the freshly compiled one. In multi-process CPU runs with Gloo collectives, asymmetric persistent cache hits then derive different `RunId`s and Gloo tags across processes, causing collectives to hang (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So let's compute `fingerprint_` with `HloModule::GetFingerprint128()` before the zero-parameter early return, matching `PjRtStreamExecutorClient`. This omits metadata from the fingerprint, avoids materializing the full HLO text in memory, and gives zero-parameter modules a valid fingerprint.

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

`GetPjRtCpuClient` populates each process's local `CpuTopology` with that worker's `process_id`, and `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()` hashes the serialized `CpuTopologyProto` directly. In homogeneous multi-process CPU jobs, every worker therefore computes a different topology fingerprint even though `process_index` has no effect on XLA:CPU compilation. Downstream caches like JAX's persistent compilation cache hash the topology fingerprint, so non-zero processes miss cache entries written by process 0 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So this change clears `process_index` on the `CpuTopologyProto` copy in `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()`, while still hashing device count, local hardware IDs, and target machine options.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that the product of non-zero dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Enforce the same `Shape::kMaxNumElements` bound in `IfrtArrayType::verify`, `VifrtArrayV1Type::verify`, and `PjRtExecutable` shape conversions, remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

display_title: PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

head_commit.message:
PR #52641: [XLA:FFI] Expose communicator rank and size through collectives

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52641

FFI host launch setup can borrow an XLA communicator but cannot read its rank and size through the public API. Expose metadata XLA already resolves so callers can select per-rank work without an additional NCCL query.

Add `Communicator::GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo(group_mode, groups, communication_id)`, returning the borrowed `communicator` handle, communicator-local `rank`, and total `size`. Keep `GetCommunicator()` as the existing handle-only query. Both use the same resolved clique.

Retain compatibility with the 0.2 C ABI for six months starting December 1, 2026. Compatibility code may be removed on or after June 1, 2027.

Executable placement (`replica_id`, `partition_id`, and their counts) is separated into !898 through the core invocation context. This MR has no dependency on that change. Process-local participant counts are not exposed.

**Validation**

External and internal wrapper tests cover returned metadata, forwarded group configuration, version handling, callback errors, and handle-only compatibility. A dedicated GPU test checks reversed participant ordering by returning each queried rank as a scalar, alongside truncated metadata arguments, untouched trailing fields, and undersized arguments. The existing public all-reduce test retains its original group helper and handle-only lookup. Source review and changed-line formatting are complete. On ComputeLab, six external API tests and two internal wrapper tests passed, and the CUDA backend library built before the final struct-size tightening. The updated two-GPU regression has not run: the ComputeLab request remained queued and was cancelled.

The focused handle-only compatibility test also passed on ComputeLab after switching to full-size arguments.
Copybara import of the project:

--
04b475d4f8091501c2393b27aeb6bc3a26dd8473 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA] Expose logical device information to FFI handlers

Let host launch setup read replica and partition coordinates and counts from the execution device assignment, without querying a communicator or transferring a scalar from the device.

--
4ba2ab5be915ccbccc6428d2636dc507dbe9644c by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA] Scope logical device lookup to the collectives extension

Expose logical coordinates through the existing GPU collective context and advance its extension version to 0.3. Remove the base FFI API and CPU changes while preserving lazy host-side lookup without requesting communication resources.

--
11c2f4ec4ffe2dbbe82ff91f6eb304b2d511df56 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA] Keep logical device docs scoped to the collectives API

Remove the standalone custom-call guide section because the guide does not otherwise document the collectives extension. Keep the accessor contract in its API headers.

--
054311ecf9109ffffed7796882cff0b0d52e5def by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA] Remove redundant extension null check from logical device lookup

--
1d6ff27d22ddde0a738d0f7a1ce7b6f642b8933d by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Expose communicator layout through the FFI collectives extension

Let host launch setup query communicator rank, size, and process-local participant count without acquiring a communicator or calling NCCL. Preserve group order and cover the metadata in the wrapper and runtime stage tests.

--
c829571bfd6ff9265c210167e22b9a42b21ae9fd by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Return communicator metadata with the handle lookup

Resolve the clique once and return its rank, size, and process-local participant count alongside the borrowed handle. Remove the separate metadata query and validate the combined result in both wrappers and the NCCL all-reduce test.

--
34117b6b0b7ee092cbd32e3354ea81df703f988a by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Preserve communicator-only FFI argument compatibility

Accept the original communicator argument prefix and write metadata only when the caller provides space. Exercise the smaller prefix and reject undersized arguments in the GPU all-reduce test.

--
380daac31fd5df47b2f1cbf581f6a7b596c6d89d by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Gate communicator metadata on the complete struct extent

Treat the metadata fields added together as one optional block. Preserve communicator-only callers and verify that a partial metadata block remains untouched.

--
46b896d9a2648abe6ffd327c1b137aa3ff4522f2 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Accept compatible collectives extension minor versions

Allow same-major runtimes from 0.2 onward while gating metadata queries that require 0.3. Document additive minor revisions and test compatibility through C++ context decoding.

f6a993d1c509ded04b9768753ccb751a36c6f5ff by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Remove redundant communicator compatibility documentation

00c338b954f230993f767aae2c35acb8dba54b6d by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Preserve the handle-only C++ communicator API

Restore GetCommunicator and add GetCommunicatorWithRankInfo for metadata. Keep handle lookup available on 0.2 runtimes and verify both APIs through the internal and external wrappers.

--
00bbcd62c4c087c7af706d50a2ee038dcf401dbc by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Match the communicator metadata type to its query name

--
c28089d414cd055d8e1847c2f30851cac60fbc83 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

Follow the updated Prepare contract so logical device validation reaches its handler in each runtime stage.

--
4e9c843cb8ace667c8dcca2fdb0f4d603a2d62e3 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Keep collective metadata scoped to communicator rank and size

Split executable placement into an independent core API change and remove the process-local participant count. Collective queries retain handle-only compatibility and no longer depend on placement metadata.

--

--
bbe0722f672941b2735429da7f7d9f0cbca32d09 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Remove custom collective version compatibility logic

Use the shared extension decoder policy and remove the metadata minor-version gate, compatibility tests, and unused test dependencies.

--
c9a725670dad8b1aab4b2ce93f74527f584d86a1 by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Restore collective version compatibility handling

--
23d195b98b7c319fe31eb7466d05bad98f62dbac by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Validate communicator metadata and argument layouts

Reject incompatible extension versions, incomplete argument layouts, and invalid rank/size results before publishing outputs. Retain the 0.2 ABI for the six-month compatibility window ending 2027-06-01.

--
c27e152b6d1f9d5760d07b99a8a24857f438b84e by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Pass full communicator arguments for handle-only lookup

Initialize rank and size to -1 and advertise the current argument layout so runtimes can populate metadata when available. Keep the handle-only return value and test compatibility with older callbacks that leave metadata unset.

--
31bffc6c2b2ac86641fdb3dd857bcda07bb1f85c by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Validate legacy argument size before checking rank fields

Reject undersized communicator arguments explicitly so has_rank_info can use a greater-than comparison while preserving legacy and full-layout validation.

--
3d526151a04c039ad44283b73066d50c32503b9b by Michael Goldfarb <mgoldfarb@nvidia.com>:

[XLA:FFI] Consolidate versioned communicator argument validation

Name the v0.2 and v0.3 layouts explicitly and validate the selected minimum size once. Gate rank metadata on the complete v0.3 layout while preserving rejection of undersized and partial arguments.

Merging this change closes #52641

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

head_commit.message:
Reuse operands through other positions if heap shrinks

`HeapSimulator::RunComputation` only lets a temporary reuse the buffer of an operand value if the user consumes the defining instruction of that value directly. A user that reads the value only through other positions (e.g. two `get-tuple-element`s of a tuple, or a bitcast) never reuses the buffer, even if every read is elementwise.

Reusing these buffers as well lowers the peak memory, but a reused buffer stays at the same offset for longer, which can increase the fragmentation by more than the reuse saves. So always reusing them makes some modules smaller and others larger.

Therefore this change adds `HeapSimulator::RunWithBeneficialOperandReuse`, which `BufferAssigner` now uses. If a heap simulation reused such a buffer, the allocs and frees are replayed without this kind of reuse (new `HeapSimulator::Options::may_reuse_operand_buffers_through_other_positions`), and the reuse is only kept if it results in a smaller heap.

Comparing the heaps needs a second `HeapAlgorithm::Finish()`, which is slow on large modules for the `kSpatial` and `kTemporal` packing strategies. So for algorithms without a fast `Finish()` (new `HeapAlgorithm::HasFastFinish()`), the reuse is dropped right away if it does not lower the peak memory. Stats-only runs (`NoFragmentationStatsHeap` in `MinimumMemoryForModule`) stay restricted to direct operands so schedule scoring in `DefaultMemoryScheduler` does not change.
