name: CI ROCm
display_title: [IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate non-negative dimensions and element-count bounds in `xla::ifrt::Shape`

Constructing an `xla::ifrt::Shape` deferred negative-dimension checks to `Shape::num_elements()` and permitted dimensions whose total element count overflowed `int64_t` or exceeded what bit-size and byte-size calculations could represent. Callers computing `shape.num_elements() * dtype.bit_size()` or `shape.num_elements() * dtype.byte_size()` could silently wrap signed `int64_t` unless every backend and utility repeated its own checked multiplication.

Add `Shape::Create` to validate non-negative dimensions and that the product of non-zero dimensions fits within `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (`INT64_MAX / 128`, accommodating elements up to 128 bits), returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` on invalid dimensions, and delegate `Shape`'s constructor (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Shape::FromProto` to `Shape::Create`. Enforce the same `Shape::kMaxNumElements` bound in `IfrtArrayType::verify`, `VifrtArrayV1Type::verify`, and `PjRtExecutable` shape conversions, remove `Shape::NumElements()`, drop redundant downstream negative-dimension and byte-size overflow checks, and update IFRT unit tests that constructed `Shape` with negative dimensions.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1021496910

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Use HloModule::GetFingerprint128 for PjRtCpuExecutable

`PjRtCpuExecutable` currently hashes `HloModule::ToString()` for its executable fingerprint and returns early before computing a fingerprint when a module has zero parameters. Default HLO printing includes `OpMetadata`, where `HloModule::CanonicalizeStackFrameIds` renumbers stack frame IDs in computation order during proto deserialization. When optimization passes introduce callee subcomputations that serialize before `ENTRY`, a deserialized executable gets a different fingerprint than the freshly compiled one. In multi-process CPU runs with Gloo collectives, asymmetric persistent cache hits then derive different `RunId`s and Gloo tags across processes, causing collectives to hang (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So let's compute `fingerprint_` with `HloModule::GetFingerprint128()` before the zero-parameter early return, matching `PjRtStreamExecutorClient`. This omits metadata from the fingerprint, avoids materializing the full HLO text in memory, and gives zero-parameter modules a valid fingerprint.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024779437

display_title: [XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Ignore process_index in CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint

`GetPjRtCpuClient` populates each process's local `CpuTopology` with that worker's `process_id`, and `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()` hashes the serialized `CpuTopologyProto` directly. In homogeneous multi-process CPU jobs, every worker therefore computes a different topology fingerprint even though `process_index` has no effect on XLA:CPU compilation. Downstream caches like JAX's persistent compilation cache hash the topology fingerprint, so non-zero processes miss cache entries written by process 0 (https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42734).

So this change clears `process_index` on the `CpuTopologyProto` copy in `CpuTopologyDescription::Fingerprint()`, while still hashing device count, local hardware IDs, and target machine options.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1024783545

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 970283402

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Fix HostOffloader CHECK failure on shared while condition computations

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fix HostOffloader CHECK failure on shared while loop condition computations

HostOffloader::ApplySchedulingFix unconditionally ran HloAliasAnalysis on the module, which fatally CHECK-fails in ComputeWhileAliasedValues when multiple while loops share a single condition computation because the call graph has not been flattened.

This change:

- Short-circuits ApplySchedulingFix if no candidate host-memory DynamicUpdateSlice instructions exist in non-entry computations, avoiding redundant alias analysis passes and memory allocations.

- If candidates exist and the call graph is not flat on control flow, runs FlattenCallGraph, invalidates the cached call_graph_ pointer (preserving the caching invariant from PR #49369), and marks changed = true before running HloAliasAnalysis.

- Adds comprehensive regression and control tests in host_offloader_test.

Fixes #50115.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Preserve sorted scatter indices when subtracting shard offsets

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Preserve sorted scatter indices when subtracting shard offsets

`PartitionScatterTrivialSlicedOperandDimensions` and `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` subtract `indices_min` in the original scatter index type while keeping `indices_are_sorted` true. On nonzero partitions, unsigned indices below `indices_min` and signed indices near the type minimum underflow to large positive values and break sortedness. When `indices_are_sorted` is true, `ClampSorted` clamps signed indices at `-1` and converts unsigned indices to `S32` or `S64` after capping at the signed maximum. Existing valid programs are unchanged.

display_title: [IFRT IR] Enforce direct `FuncOp` nesting in `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` and simplify IFRT IR passes

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Enforce direct `FuncOp` nesting in `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` and simplify IFRT IR passes

Operations carrying `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` were silently accepted outside any function (such as directly inside a `builtin.module`) because the trait verifier only checked function attributes when an enclosing `func.func` was found. Walking up to any enclosing function via `getParentOfType` also allowed IFRT ops to appear inside nested regions such as `stablehlo.if`.

Tighten `NestedInIfrtFuncTrait` to require the direct parent to be a `func.func` with `ifrt.function` or `ifrt.reshard_function`, rejecting unenclosed and nested-region ops, and fix the `atttr` typo in the diagnostic message.

Combined with the single-block body invariant on IFRT functions, every IFRT op is now guaranteed to live directly in the entry block of its enclosing function. Simplify IFRT IR import and compilation passes to scan function operations directly instead of recursively walking nested regions.

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Preserve sorted scatter indices when subtracting shard offsets

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Preserve sorted scatter indices when subtracting shard offsets

`PartitionScatterTrivialSlicedOperandDimensions` and `HandleScatterWithoutConflicts` subtract `indices_min` in the original scatter index type while keeping `indices_are_sorted` true. On nonzero partitions, unsigned indices below `indices_min` and signed indices near the type minimum underflow to large positive values and break sortedness. When `indices_are_sorted` is true, `ClampSorted` clamps signed indices at `-1` and converts unsigned indices to `S32` or `S64` after capping at the signed maximum. Existing valid programs are unchanged.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [IFRT IR] Tighten `IfrtDialect` attribute and `IfrtArrayType` verifiers

head_commit.message:
[IFRT IR] Tighten `IfrtDialect` operation, region-arg, and region-result attribute verifiers

Most `ifrt.*` attributes were not validated by the dialect verifier, which only checked `ifrt.function` on operations and `ifrt.donated` on region arguments while leaving region-result attribute verification disabled. Because malformed attributes and function bodies could slip past parsing, downstream passes had to carry defensive guards for empty or multi-block IFRT functions, unknown `ifrt.module_type` values, and inconsistent `ifrt.local_view` lookups.

Enabling region-result attribute verification and enforcing dialect-level invariants for known `ifrt.*` attributes closes those gaps while leaving unrecognized `ifrt.*` op, argument, and result attributes permitted for serialized bytecode compatibility:

* `ifrt.function` and `ifrt.reshard_function` must be mutually exclusive `UnitAttr`s on `func.func` ops nested directly in a `builtin.module`, with a single-block body ending in `func.return` and restricted to `!ifrt.array` / `!ifrt.control` types (strictly `!ifrt.array` types and resharding ops for `ifrt.reshard_function`).
* `ifrt.local_view`, `ifrt.module_type` (`"xla"` or `"mpmd_reshard"`), `ifrt.compile_options_key`, `ifrt.num_devices` (positive `i32`), and `ifrt.mesh_name` are validated for their allowed host ops and values.
* `ifrt.donated` is restricted to `!ifrt.array` arguments of `ifrt.function` ops (and rejected on results), while `ifrt.sharding`, `ifrt.devices`, and `ifrt.memory_kind` are validated on both `func.func` region arguments and region results.

Downstream passes and tests are simplified accordingly by removing redundant single-block/non-empty guards, unknown `ifrt.module_type` error branches, dead function-level `ifrt.*` attribute removals, and typed `ifrt.local_view` checks.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026107426

display_title: [IFRT] Validate element bounds and non-zero product in `xla::ifrt::Index`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate element bounds and non-zero product in `xla::ifrt::Index`

`Index` only rejected negative elements inside `Index::FromProto`, leaving direct C++ construction via `Index(elements)` and arithmetic via `operator+`, `operator-`, and `operator*` able to produce negative, overflow-wrapped, or unreachable coordinates whose cumulative non-zero element product exceeds `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (and thus cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`).

Add `Index::Create` returning `absl::InvalidArgumentError` if any element is negative or if the cumulative product of non-zero elements exceeds `Shape::kMaxNumElements`, delegate both `Index(elements)` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `Index::FromProto` to `Index::Create`, and `CHECK` that `Index::Zeros` and `Index` arithmetic operators preserve non-negativity and the non-zero product bound without underflow or overflow. Update `IndexDomainTest.Contains` and `array_slice_impl_test_lib` to avoid constructing `Index` instances with negative coordinates.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched numbers of dimensions and allowed `origin[i] + shape.dims()[i]` (and their cumulative non-zero product) to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` or overflow `int64_t`, forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand checks on the number of dimensions while allowing domains that cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and that the cumulative product of non-zero upper-bound dimensions (`origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]`) does not exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements`, delegate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `IndexDomain::FromProto` to `IndexDomain::Create`, and route `operator+=` / `operator-=` through `operator+` / `operator-` so offset mutations preserve upper-bound validity.

Add optional variadic ext_operands with block_scaling_config and
sparsity_config attributes to mhlo.dot_general, mirroring

stablehlo_legalize_to_hlo.

require both configs to be absent, so they keep handling only plain dots.

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` and compile-only `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile`

`IfrtIrProgramCompiler` currently implements `CompileAndLoad`, while `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile(program, topology, options)` has no compiled `Executable` representation for holding a lowered IFRT IR module and its unloaded atom programs prior to `Client::Load`.

Introduce `IfrtIrExecutable` (`RTTIExtends<IfrtIrExecutable, Executable>`) to own the lowered `IfrtIRProgram` in a dedicated `MLIRContext` (parsing per-load `MLIRContext` instances from pre-serialized MLIR bytecode in `CreateCompiledIfrtIrProgram` so concurrent `Client::Load` calls do not mutate the shared `MLIRContext`), expose its compiled atom programs and metadata queries, and wire `IfrtIrProgramCompiler::Compile` to `IfrtIrExecutable::Create`. Target device resolution continues to use the compiler's `Client*` and `IfrtIRCompileOptions::device_assignments`, and `Client::Load` support for `IfrtIrExecutable` lands in a follow-up change.

head_commit.message:
[PJRT] Fix StreamExecutor clients picking host callbacks by replica instead of device index

This fixes a bug that the StreamExecutor client picked the host callbacks of a device by its replica. `ExecuteOptions::send_callbacks` and `recv_callbacks` have one entry for each device of the execution: one for each addressable device with `Execute`, and a single one with `ExecuteSharded` or `ExecutePortable`. The replica is only the same as that index when `Execute` runs one partition with all replicas on this host.

For example, the new test compiles a program with 2 replicas and runs only replica 1 with `ExecuteSharded`, so it passes one entry. The client looked up entry 1 and failed with "no send callbacks registered for the replica=1".

The client now uses the device index that the common code already passes, like the TPU client.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:PjRt] Add 512 bit transpose microkernels and runtime block sizing

head_commit.message:
[XLA:PjRt] Add 512 bit transpose microkernels and runtime block sizing

`TransposePlan` previously capped vectorized inner blocks at 16 or 32 bytes at
compile time and lacked 512 bit Highway transpose kernels. Partial remainder
tiles also fell directly back to scalar element copies.

Add spill free 512 bit transpose microkernels in `xla/pjrt/transpose_kernels.cc`
covering 64 byte, 32 byte, and 16 byte rows with sequential row stores. Select
square, half, or strip kernels by target and stride alignment to avoid L1D set
thrashing. Keep Zen 4 narrow element blocks within 256 bit halves to avoid
double pumped cross lane permutes. Select the inner block byte limit from the
active Highway target at runtime, leaving 16 byte elements at scalar block size.
Recursively halve partial remainder tiles into smaller power of two SIMD blocks
down to 16 byte rows. Existing transpose outputs are bit identical and no flags
are added.

head_commit.message:
Add `GpuDmaBufCache` for suballocator chunk-level Linux dma-buf fd caching.

Caching exported dma-buf fds per suballocator chunk avoids per-buffer driver
export overhead and file descriptor exhaustion under high concurrency, while
`free_visitor` invalidation ensures fds are closed before the backing memory is
freed. Allocations outside tracked chunks (or spanning multiple chunks) fall
back to an uncached RAII export.

display_title: Ignore dynamic shape metadata prefix for static inputs and PadRealToStatic parameters in CheckBufferCompatibilities.

head_commit.message:
Ignore dynamic shape metadata prefix for static inputs and PadRealToStatic parameters in CheckBufferCompatibilities.

When `CommonPjRtLoadedExecutable::CheckBufferCompatibilities` validates parameter layouts on TPU, two valid dynamic-shape execution cases can have differing dynamic metadata prefixes between the expected parameter shape and the actual input buffer: passing an unprefixed static buffer to an executable with a dynamic parameter, and passing a dynamic buffer with an in-buffer metadata prefix to a `PadRealToStatic` parameter whose expected device shape is unprefixed.

Extract two helper functions to accept unprefixed static buffers for dynamic parameters and prefixed dynamic buffers for `PadRealToStatic` parameters, while rejecting static buffers carrying a non-matching prefix and guarding layoutless or non-array shapes. Also check when the actual shape doesn't have a layout or the layout doesn't have a metadata prefix when deciding whether runtime bounds checks are external, validate dynamic buffer dimensions passed to static parameter dimensions, and reject negative runtime dimension sizes.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

head_commit.message:
Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

**Problem:**
When post-scheduling `CopyRemover` deletes a copy so that an old value (`src`) and a new value (`dst`) share the same physical buffer, it must add a control dependency from every reader of `src` to the instruction that writes `dst`. This prevents later passes (such as `HloRematerialization`) from moving or cloning a read of `src` past the point where `dst` overwrites the shared buffer.

For asynchronous operations (such as `dynamic-slice-start`), the output value `dst` is defined by the inner instruction inside the child `async_wrapped_computation`, not in the parent computation. Previously:
1. When checking *whether* the copy could be deleted, `LiveRangeBefore` resolved the inner async instruction to its `kAsyncStart` caller in the parent computation and approved sharing the buffer.
2. However, when adding the control dependency *after* deleting the copy, `add_control_deps` saw that the reader of `src` (in the parent computation) and the inner async instruction (in the child computation) had different `parent()` computations, and silently skipped adding the control edge.

Without that control dependency, `HloRematerialization` could clone a reader of `src` to a point in the schedule after `kAsyncStart`, causing it to read the shared buffer while the background async DMA was overwriting it.

**Fix:**
1. In `add_control_deps`, when the reader and writer belong to different computations, resolve instructions inside an async computation to their `kAsyncStart` caller so the control dependency (`reader_of_src -> kAsyncStart`) is added in the parent computation (while preserving intra-computation edges inside multi-instruction async computations).
2. Check `ordering_->ExecutesBefore(use_instr, dst_instr)` before adding the edge so that in-place async operations (where `src->uses` also includes `kAsyncDone` / `kAsyncUpdate`, which executes *after* `kAsyncStart`) do not add a backward control edge from `kAsyncDone` back to `kAsyncStart`.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched numbers of dimensions and allowed `origin[i] + shape.dims()[i]` (and their cumulative non-zero product) to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` or overflow `int64_t`, forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand checks on the number of dimensions while allowing domains that cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and that the cumulative product of non-zero upper-bound dimensions (`origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i]`) does not exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements`, delegate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `IndexDomain::FromProto` to `IndexDomain::Create`, and route `operator+=` / `operator-=` through `operator+` / `operator-` so offset mutations preserve upper-bound validity.

display_title: PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

head_commit.message:
PR #52240: [XLA:GPU] Preserve frontend attributes in dot rewriters

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/52240

:pencil: **Summary of Changes**

Preserve frontend attributes when dot rewriters replace a dot with new instructions. New dots are added with `HloInstruction::AddInstruction` on the original dot, which derives them via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (also carrying metadata and, where shapes allow, sharding, like existing rewriters such as `DotDimensionSorter`), so they inherit the original dot's frontend attributes instead of silently dropping them. This covers `DotAlgorithmRewriter` (the BF16/TF32 decompositions in `backends/gpu/transforms` and the FP8xN decomposition in `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter.cc`), `ScaledDotRewriter`, `SplitkRewriter`, and `GemmFusionSwapOperands`.

:dart: **Justification**

Frontend attributes are the mechanism by which the frontend (e.g. JAX) attaches annotations to HLO instructions for downstream passes to consume. When a pass replaces an instruction, it must carry those attributes over to the replacement; otherwise the annotation is silently dropped and the consumers that depend on it no longer see it. These dot rewriters were not doing this, so annotated matmuls lost their scheduling annotations.

:compass: **Design: deriving replacements from the original dot**

Each new dot is added with `original_dot->AddInstruction(...)`, which derives it via `SetupDerivedInstruction` (metadata, frontend attributes, and sharding where the shapes allow). Instructions built by helpers call `SetupDerivedInstruction` directly: the instruction that replaces the dot in `RewriteDotWithOperandPairs` (shared by BF16X3/X6/X9 and TF32X3) and `RewriteFp8xNDot` (FP8X3/X4), and the split-K dot, which `MakeDotHlo` creates. So every new dot and the instruction that replaces the original keep the annotation.

:rocket: **Kind of Contribution**

:bug: Bug Fix

:test_tube: **Unit Tests:**

Added hardware-independent tests asserting frontend attributes survive each dot rewrite:

* `backends/gpu/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `KeepsFrontendAttributes`, parameterized over every `PrecisionConfig::Algorithm`: verifies that after the pass every dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep the attributes. Without the fix it fails for the seven algorithms the pass decomposes (BF16, BF16X3/X6/X9, TF32X3, FP8X3/X4); new algorithms are covered automatically.
* `hlo/transforms/dot_algorithm_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewriteFp8xNDotStructureTest.KeepsFrontendAttributes`, for FP8X3 and FP8X4 at both precisions: verifies every F8 dot and the instruction that replaces the dot keep them.
* `gemm_fusion_swap_operands_test.cc`:
  * `SwappedDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the swapped dot keeps them.
* `scaled_dot_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `RewrittenDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the dot replacing a scaled-dot keeps them.
* `splitk_rewriter_test.cc`:
  * `SplitKDotKeepsFrontendAttributes`: verifies the split-K dot keeps them.

:test_tube: **Execution Tests:**

No new checked-in execution test was added.

display_title: Avoid dereferencing end() in HloSharding::GetSubSharding.

head_commit.message:
Avoid dereferencing end() in HloSharding::GetSubSharding.

`HloSharding::GetSubSharding` constructed a subspan of `tuple_elements_` by
taking `&*begin_it` and `&*(begin_it + leaf_count)`. When the sub-tuple extends
to the end of `tuple_elements_` or is an empty tuple, this dereferences
`tuple_elements_.end()`, which is undefined behavior and traps under libc++
bounded iterators.

Slice `absl::MakeConstSpan(tuple_elements_).subspan(sharding_index, leaf_count)`
instead, after checking `sharding_index + leaf_count <= tuple_elements_.size()`.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

head_commit.message:
[XLA:CPU] Do not offload 8-bit integer arithmetic to YNNPACK

With default flags, porting a `uint8` image pipeline to JAX on CPU gives
results that differ from NumPy and XLA:GPU as soon as the inputs are large
enough to be fused into a `__ynn_fusion`. For example:

```python
f = jax.jit(lambda a, b: jnp.max(a, axis=0, keepdims=True) + b)
f(np.full((1024, 17), 255, np.uint8), np.full((1024, 17), 103, np.uint8))
```

returns `255` instead of `102`, and in a `uint8` contrast stretch 50-89% of
the pixels on 480x640 frames are wrong. `s8` `127 + 1` gives `127` instead of
`-128`, and `s8` `7 / 2` gives `4` instead of `3`. XLA:GPU, NumPy,
`HloEvaluator`, constant folding and XLA:CPU on small (unfused) inputs all
wrap and truncate.

Reported by @SomyaPadhy4501 in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/51826
(found while porting an image pipeline, and also by a CPU-vs-GPU integer
fuzzer).

Root cause: `IsElementwiseOpSupportedByYnn` accepts `S8`/`U8` for every op in
`GetYnnBinaryOpMap()`. YNNPACK's 8-bit add, subtract and multiply saturate and
its integer divide rounds, so any of these ops fused next to a YNN reduction
(the default `REDUCE` fusion type) changes the result.

Fix: for `S8`/`U8` binary ops, only offload `maximum` and `minimum`, which give
the same results either way. Other 8-bit binary ops fall back to the regular
XLA:CPU emitter. Floating-point ops, integer reductions, converts and unary
ops are unchanged. This follows the earlier fixes that stop offloading ops
YNNPACK cannot compute exactly (#48378, #49899).

Tested: new `YnnReduceInt8EltwiseTest.EltwiseAfterReduceWraps` in
`//xla/backends/cpu/transforms:ynn_matcher_test` runs the issue's pattern
(max/min reduce + broadcast + add/subtract/multiply/divide on `u8`/`s8`
`[1024,17]`). All 5 cases fail before this change (255 vs 102, 127 vs -128,
0 vs 255, 127 vs -56, 4 vs 3) and pass after it.
`YnnReduceTest.Int8MaximumAfterReduceIsFused` checks that `s8` maximum is
still fused into `__ynn_fusion`.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026635721

When `MismatchDetails::has_element_level_data` is `false` (such as in SparseCore mismatch dumps), `ClearElementLevelData` clears `shape` and sets `total_elements = 0`, causing `isInspectableTensor` to return `false`. name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

head_commit.message:
Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

**Problem:**
When post-scheduling `CopyRemover` deletes a copy so that an old value (`src`) and a new value (`dst`) share the same physical buffer, it must add a control dependency from every reader of `src` to the instruction that writes `dst`. This prevents later passes (such as `HloRematerialization`) from moving or cloning a read of `src` past the point where `dst` overwrites the shared buffer.

For asynchronous operations (such as `dynamic-slice-start`), the output value `dst` is defined by the inner instruction inside the child `async_wrapped_computation`, not in the parent computation. Previously:
1. When checking *whether* the copy could be deleted, `LiveRangeBefore` resolved the inner async instruction to its `kAsyncStart` caller in the parent computation and approved sharing the buffer.
2. However, when adding the control dependency *after* deleting the copy, `add_control_deps` saw that the reader of `src` (in the parent computation) and the inner async instruction (in the child computation) had different `parent()` computations, and silently skipped adding the control edge.

Without that control dependency, `HloRematerialization` could clone a reader of `src` to a point in the schedule after `kAsyncStart`, causing it to read the shared buffer while the background async DMA was overwriting it.

**Fix:**
1. In `add_control_deps`, resolve instructions inside an async computation to their `kAsyncStart` caller so the control dependency (`reader_of_src -> kAsyncStart`) is added in the parent computation.
2. Check `ordering_->ExecutesBefore(use_instr, dst_instr)` before adding the edge so that in-place async operations (where `src->uses` also includes `kAsyncDone` / `kAsyncUpdate`, which executes *after* `kAsyncStart`) do not add a backward control edge from `kAsyncDone` back to `kAsyncStart`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010199447

display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Bitcast F8E8M0FNU to U8 in trivial slice gather partitioning

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Bitcast F8E8M0FNU to U8 in trivial slice gather partitioning

When a gather operand is partitioned along trivial slice dimensions, `PartitionGatherTrivialSlicedOperandDimensions` and `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::HandleGatherWithoutConflicts` mask out of bounds shards with `CreateZero`. Both paths then sum masked local gather results across partitions using `AllReduceAlongShardingDims` and `MakeBinaryAdd`. Because `F8E8M0FNU` lacks a zero representation, `LiteralUtil::Zero(F8E8M0FNU)` produces raw byte `0x00`, encoding `2^-127` rather than `0`. Summing `F8E8M0FNU` shards against `0x00` lacks an additive identity, doubling `2^-127` values or flushing subnormal mask sums to `NaN`. Move `BitcastTo` from `spmd_partitioner.cc` into `spmd_partitioner_util.h` so `Broadcast`, `ReplicatePartial`, and gather partitioning share one helper. Bitcast `F8E8M0FNU` local gather outputs to `U8` before zero masking and `all-reduce`, then bitcast the reduced `U8` result back to `F8E8M0FNU`. All other element types remain unchanged, with no flag.

display_title: [XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SDY] Support JAX custom_partitioning in Shardy partitioner

When the Shardy partitioner is fully enabled, GSPMD is completely bypassed,
leaving `stablehlo.custom_call @CustomSPMDPartitioning` unpartitioned and
failing compilation. To support it, we change the following:

- **Partitioner-agnostic callback API**: Add
  `CustomCallPartitioner::SupportsMlirPartitioning()` and `PartitionToMlir()`
  (defaulting to `false` / `std::nullopt` for GSPMD-only C++ partitioners),
  share PJRT C-API callback marshaling in `CApiCustomCallPartitioner` between
  GSPMD and Shardy, and remove the now-unused HLO-based `PopulateArgs`
  overload.

- **Callback MLIR preparation & sharding import**: Extract shared tile
  factorization (`factorizeTileAssignmentToSdy`) into
  `stablehlo_round_trip/sharding_import_utils.{h,cc}`, handle matching-mesh V3
  `NamedSharding` directly with V2 fallback, upgrade VHLO, inline direct helper
  calls, and legalize CHLO and complex math in a single `PassManager`, remapping
  positive `channel_handle` IDs via `nextChannelId` and importing remaining
  private helpers (such as `stablehlo.composite` decompositions) into
  `symbolTable`.

- **Global-IR lowering (`resolvePermutationFactors`)**: Wire
  `custom_spmd_partitioning.{h,cc}` into `CustomCallPartitioningOpInterface`,
  rewriting custom-partitioned calls into operand `sdy.reshard` (when needed) +
  divisibility padding + `sdy.manual_computation` + slicing + result
  `sdy.reshard` (when needed).

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

head_commit.message:
Add post-scheduling control dependencies to async callers in CopyRemover.

**Problem:**
When post-scheduling `CopyRemover` deletes a copy so that an old value (`src`) and a new value (`dst`) share the same physical buffer, it must add a control dependency from every reader of `src` to the instruction that writes `dst`. This prevents later passes (such as `HloRematerialization`) from moving or cloning a read of `src` past the point where `dst` overwrites the shared buffer.

For asynchronous operations (such as `dynamic-slice-start`), the output value `dst` is defined by the inner instruction inside the child `async_wrapped_computation`, not in the parent computation. Previously:
1. When checking *whether* the copy could be deleted, `LiveRangeBefore` resolved the inner async instruction to its `kAsyncStart` caller in the parent computation and approved sharing the buffer.
2. However, when adding the control dependency *after* deleting the copy, `add_control_deps` saw that the reader of `src` (in the parent computation) and the inner async instruction (in the child computation) had different `parent()` computations, and silently skipped adding the control edge.

Without that control dependency, `HloRematerialization` could clone a reader of `src` to a point in the schedule after `kAsyncStart`, causing it to read the shared buffer while the background async DMA was overwriting it.

**Fix:**
1. In `add_control_deps`, resolve instructions inside an async computation to their `kAsyncStart` caller so the control dependency (`reader_of_src -> kAsyncStart`) is added in the parent computation.
2. Check `ordering_->ExecutesBefore(use_instr, dst_instr)` before adding the edge so that in-place async operations (where `src->uses` also includes `kAsyncDone` / `kAsyncUpdate`, which executes *after* `kAsyncStart`) do not add a backward control edge from `kAsyncDone` back to `kAsyncStart`.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1010199447

display_title: [XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

A JAX user jitting `jnp.concatenate([a[i], a[i+1:i+2]])` on CPU gets `[6. 6.]`
instead of `[5. 6.]` (jaxlib 0.7.1 through 0.12.1; correct with
`--xla_disable_hlo_passes=fusion`). Reported in
https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42758 and
https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/53472.

After optimization the gather becomes a dynamic-slice, so the fused concatenate
has two operands named `dynamic-slice.N` and `dynamic_slice.N`. The concatenate
emitter makes every concatenate operand its own subgraph. `PartitionedComputation`
names each subgraph `<computation>_<roots>` and passes it through
`llvm_ir::SanitizeFunctionName`, which turns both `-` and `.` into `_`. Both
operands end up with the same `func.func` name, so both call sites resolve to the
same function. With MLIR verification on this fails with
`redefinition of symbol named 'fused_computation_dynamic_slice_0'`. Without it,
both slots silently read the same operand.

The fix adds a `_<k>` suffix in the `PartitionedComputation` constructor when a
sanitized subgraph name is already taken. This matches the documented contract
of `Subgraph::name` ("A unique name of the subgraph. Used for function names.").
Names that do not collide are unchanged. The CPU and GPU emitters share this
code, so both get the fix.

Tests:
- `ComputationPartitionerTest.SubgraphNamesAreUniqueAfterSanitization`: checks
  that the two colliding roots get distinct names.
- `ConcatenateTest.FusedOperandsWithCollidingSanitizedNames`: end-to-end HLO
  execution test that expects `[5, 6]`. Without the fix it fails on CPU with the
  symbol redefinition error.

display_title: [IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

head_commit.message:
[IFRT] Validate matching number of dimensions and bounded upper bounds in `IndexDomain`

`IndexDomain` permitted `origin` and `shape` with mismatched numbers of dimensions and allowed `origin[i] + shape.dims()[i]` to exceed `Shape::kMaxNumElements` (and even overflow `int64_t`), forcing `Intersect` and `Contains` to repeat per-operand checks on the number of dimensions while allowing slices that cannot fit inside any valid `Shape`. In addition, `IndexDomain(Shape shape)` passed both `Index::Zeros(shape.dims().size())` and `std::move(shape)` in the same delegating constructor call, relying on unspecified C++ argument evaluation order.

Add `IndexDomain::Create` to validate `origin.elements().size() == shape.dims().size()` and `origin.elements()[i] + shape.dims()[i] <= Shape::kMaxNumElements`, delegate `IndexDomain(origin, shape)` (via `CHECK_OK`) and `IndexDomain::FromProto` to `IndexDomain::Create`, initialize `origin_` and `shape_` directly in `IndexDomain(Shape shape)`, and route `operator+=` / `operator-=` through `operator+` / `operator-` so offset mutations preserve upper-bound validity.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Keep the dot algorithm when importing 2-D dots to StableHLO

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Keep the dot algorithm when importing 2-D dots to StableHLO

**Why**

A sharded `jax.jit` program partitioned with Shardy (the default partitioner)
that calls `jnp.dot(a, b, precision=jax.lax.DotAlgorithmPreset.F32_F32_F32)`
on 2-D operands silently runs at default precision. On GPU that is TF32: the
relative error is 2.9e-4 instead of 2.9e-7. `TF32_TF32_F32_X3` and
`BF16_BF16_F32_X6` show the same error. With GSPMD the results are correct.
Reported in https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/53163.

**Root cause**

Shardy round-trips the module through StableHLO. On import,
`HloFunctionImporter` turns a dot with default dimension numbers (vector or
matrix operands, no batch dimensions) into `stablehlo.dot`. `stablehlo.dot` has
no `algorithm` attribute, so the algorithm is only kept as a discardable
attribute, and the export to HLO drops it. Dots with batch dimensions already
import as `stablehlo.dot_general`, which keeps the algorithm.

**Fix**

`DotIsDefault` now returns false for a dot with an algorithm. Such dots take the
existing `stablehlo.dot_general` path, the same path batched algorithm dots
already use. Dots without an algorithm still import as `stablehlo.dot`. A 2-D
dot with an algorithm still exports to an HLO `dot` with the same dimension
numbers, and now keeps its algorithm.

**Testing**

Added `xla/hlo/translate/tests/dot_algorithm_import.hlo`. It checks that a 2-D
dot with `algorithm=dot_f32_f32_f32` imports as `stablehlo.dot_general` with the
algorithm, and that the algorithm is still there after HLO -> StableHLO -> HLO.
The test fails without the fix.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026602448

display_title: [XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

head_commit.message:
[XLA:Codegen] Make emitter subgraph function names unique after sanitization

A JAX user jitting `jnp.concatenate([a[i], a[i+1:i+2]])` on CPU gets `[6. 6.]`
instead of `[5. 6.]` (jaxlib 0.7.1 through 0.12.1; correct with
`--xla_disable_hlo_passes=fusion`). Reported in
https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42758 and
https://github.com/openxla/xla/issues/53472.

After optimization the gather becomes a dynamic-slice, so the fused concatenate
has two operands named `dynamic-slice.N` and `dynamic_slice.N`. The concatenate
emitter makes every concatenate operand its own subgraph. `PartitionedComputation`
names each subgraph `<computation>_<roots>` and passes it through
`llvm_ir::SanitizeFunctionName`, which turns both `-` and `.` into `_`. Both
operands end up with the same `func.func` name, so both call sites resolve to the
same function. With MLIR verification on this fails with
`redefinition of symbol named 'fused_computation_dynamic_slice_0'`. Without it,
both slots silently read the same operand.

The fix adds a `_<k>` suffix in the `PartitionedComputation` constructor when a
sanitized subgraph name is already taken. This matches the documented contract
of `Subgraph::name` ("A unique name of the subgraph. Used for function names.").
Names that do not collide are unchanged. The CPU and GPU emitters share this
code, so both get the fix.

Tests:
- `ComputationPartitionerTest.SubgraphNamesAreUniqueAfterSanitization`: checks
  that the two colliding roots get distinct names.
- `ConcatenateTest.FusedOperandsWithCollidingSanitizedNames`: end-to-end HLO
  execution test that expects `[5, 6]`. Without the fix it fails on CPU with the
  symbol redefinition error.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Mask nonzero shards on unindexed gather trivial slice dims

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Mask nonzero shards on unindexed gather trivial slice dims

In `HandleGatherWithoutConflicts` and
`PartitionGatherTrivialSlicedOperandDimensions`, an operand dimension with slice
size one that is absent from `start_index_map` has an implicit global start
index of zero. Previously,
`IndexBoundsForGatherScatterOperandPartitionedOnTrivialSliceDims` checked only
dimensions listed in `start_index_map`. Shards with a nonzero partition offset
along an unindexed trivial slice dimension were not masked out before the cross
partition `all-reduce`, summing values from nonzero shards into the gather
result.

Include unindexed trivial slice dimensions in
`GatherOperandPartitionedOnTrivialSliceDims` and mask out shards whose partition
offset along any unindexed trivial slice dimension is nonzero using an element
type matching `MakePartitionOffsets`. When `start_index_map` is empty, skip
index clamping, offset adjustment, and index bounds comparison, and initialize
the gather mask to `false` before `MaskUnindexedTrivialSliceDims`. Existing
programs without unindexed partitioned trivial slice dimensions do not change.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Fold identity dynamic-update-slice of slice from same source

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fold identity dynamic-update-slice of slice from same source

`AlgebraicSimplifier` did not simplify a `dynamic-update-slice` that writes an
unmodified `slice` or `dynamic-slice` of its base operand back to the same
indices. Such updates act as noops but survive into buffer assignment and force
unnecessary copies and fusions.

Fold `dynamic-update-slice(x, slice(x, starts, limits, 1), starts)` and
`dynamic-update-slice(x, dynamic-slice(x, starts, sizes), starts)` directly to
`x` in `HandleDynamicUpdateSlice`. Both `dynamic-slice` and
`dynamic-update-slice` clamp each start index to the same range, so dynamic
offsets fold with exact bit equality. Also look through `reshape` and `bitcast`
operations that only insert or delete size 1 dimensions while preserving
physical element order and tiling (checked via
`ShapeUtil::ReshapePreservesTiledLayout`). Guard against dynamic shapes, buffer
shapes, layout or sharding mismatches, and control predecessors via
`ReplaceInstructionIfCompatible`. Existing program outputs are unchanged.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test` pins static
  slice, dynamic slice, degenerate size 1 reshape and bitcast folds, and
  rejection of strided, shifted, transposing, retiling, dynamic, resharding,
  control dependent, and layout mismatching updates.
- `//xla:shape_util_test` pins tiled layout preservation across reshapes.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

head_commit.message:
Add buffer donation recovery to IFRT and jax.experimental.

When a JIT-compiled computation donates input buffers and fails before device execution begins (for example, due to a failed cross-host transfer or slice failure), surviving devices may still hold intact input buffers even though the caller's donated `jax.Array` handles have already been invalidated. Without runtime recovery, callers must restore donated state from a host snapshot or checkpoint.

Plumb PJRT's donation recovery future through IFRT (`ExecuteOptions::fill_recovery_future` and `LoadedExecutable::ExecuteResult::recovery_future`), reconstituting recovered per-device `PjRtBuffer`s into `ifrt::Array`s in `PjRtLoadedExecutable`. Expose `jax.experimental.donation_recovery.DonationRecovery` to wrap a single JIT or AOT-compiled call: on success `future().get()` returns `None`, on recoverable failure it reconstructs the input `(args, kwargs)` PyTree with newly wrapped arrays at recovered donated leaves and original values elsewhere, and on unrecoverable failure it raises the execution error.

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026565904

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA:SPMD] Bitcast F8E8M0FNU to U8 in trivial slice gather partitioning

head_commit.message:
[XLA:SPMD] Bitcast F8E8M0FNU to U8 in trivial slice gather partitioning

When a gather operand is partitioned along trivial slice dimensions, `PartitionGatherTrivialSlicedOperandDimensions` and `SpmdPartitioningVisitor::HandleGatherWithoutConflicts` mask out of bounds shards with `CreateZero`. Both paths then sum masked local gather results across partitions using `AllReduceAlongShardingDims` and `MakeBinaryAdd`. Because `F8E8M0FNU` lacks a zero representation, `LiteralUtil::Zero(F8E8M0FNU)` produces raw byte `0x00`, encoding `2^-127` rather than `0`. Summing `F8E8M0FNU` shards against `0x00` lacks an additive identity, doubling `2^-127` values or flushing subnormal mask sums to `NaN`. Move `BitcastTo` from `spmd_partitioner.cc` into `spmd_partitioner_util.h` so `Broadcast`, `ReplicatePartial`, and gather partitioning share one helper. Bitcast `F8E8M0FNU` local gather outputs to `U8` before zero masking and `all-reduce`, then bitcast the reduced `U8` result back to `F8E8M0FNU`. All other element types remain unchanged, with no flag.

display_title: [MHLO] Extend mhlo.dot_general with block scaling and structured sparsity

head_commit.message:
[MHLO] Extend mhlo.dot_general with block scaling and structured sparsity

Add optional variadic ext_operands with block_scaling_config and
sparsity_config attributes to mhlo.dot_general, mirroring
stablehlo.dot_general, and convert them in hlo_legalize_to_stablehlo and
stablehlo_legalize_to_hlo.

The MHLO verifier uses the shared hlo::verifyDotGeneralExtensions, so MHLO
and StableHLO accept the same configs.

TableGen patterns that build or match mhlo.dot_general in TF and TFLite are
updated for the new arguments. Builders pass no extra operands, and matchers
require both configs to be absent, so they keep handling only plain dots.

Tests:
- mlir_hlo Dialect/mhlo/hlo-legalize-to-stablehlo.mlir and

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Fold identity dynamic-update-slice of slice from same source

`AlgebraicSimplifier` did not simplify a `dynamic-update-slice` that writes an
unmodified `slice` or `dynamic-slice` of its base operand back to the same

physical element order and tiling (checked via
`ShapeUtil::ReshapePreservesTiledLayout`). Guard against dynamic shapes, buffer
shapes, layout or sharding mismatches, and control predecessors via
`ReplaceInstructionIfCompatible`. Existing program outputs are unchanged.

- `//xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test` pins static
  slice, dynamic slice, degenerate size 1 reshape and bitcast folds, and
  rejection of strided, shifted, transposing, retiling, dynamic, resharding,
  control dependent, and layout mismatching updates.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Redirect only aliasing uses when copying shared read only values

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Redirect only aliasing uses when copying shared read only values

When `CopyRemover` elides one of several copies of a constant or unaliased
entry parameter, that read only value joins a buffer with other values.
`CopyInsertion::AddSpecialCaseCopies` previously inserted a fresh copy and
replaced every use of the read only instruction. That rewrite turned every
other surviving copy into a double copy chain and routed pure read only
consumers through the new copy, extending its live range.

Record unaliased array uses that read an isolated read only value directly or
through unrooted `kGetTupleElement` and same memory space `kBitcast` ops with
no control dependencies, excluding views, `Pin`, in place slots, value
forwarding ops, and control flow calls. After `DeepCopyInstruction` redirects
aliasing uses to the fresh copy, restore those recorded uses onto the original
read only value (cloning a shared `kBitcast` when needed) and update active
schedules. Each read only value stays in a singleton `HloBuffer`. Copies
requested by `custom_buffer_analysis` or disallowed operand sharing still
replace all uses.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:copy_insertion_test`: verifies shared constants, read
  only array and tuple entry parameters, shared bitcasts, controlled tuple
  elements, view colors, custom buffer callbacks, and scheduled modules.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026463116

name: CI ROCm
display_title: [XLA] Hoist loop invariant layout changing copies in LICM

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Hoist loop invariant layout changing copies in LICM

When `WhileLoopInvariantCodeMotion` runs after layout assignment and fusion
with `hoist_reshapes` enabled and `hoist_other` disabled, it skips every opcode
other than `kConstant` and `kReshape`. That leaves unfused layout changing
`kCopy` instructions and decomposed `kBitcast` to `kCopy` or `kReshape` chains
executing inside the loop body on every iteration.

Allow `WhileLoopInvariantCodeMotion` to hoist layout changing array `kCopy`
instructions in the default memory space under `hoist_reshapes`. Also trace
through default memory space `kBitcast` operands that feed a hoisted copy or
reshape. Same layout buffer isolation copies and copies or bitcasts in any
nondefault memory space are never hoisted. Standalone bitcasts without a
hoisted user remain in the loop body and add no tuple state. The size inflation
check evaluates in double precision over layout aware shape sizes and rejects
copies that expand padded storage.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:while_loop_invariant_code_motion_test` pins layout copy
  and bitcast chain hoisting, attribute preservation, `CopyInsertion`, same
  layout and nondefault memory space rejection, and size inflation limits.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026446241

display_title: [XLA] Peel bitcasts when checking buffer aliasing in ShouldFuseInPlaceOp

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Peel bitcasts when checking buffer aliasing in ShouldFuseInPlaceOp

`InstructionFusion::ShouldFuseInPlaceOp` compared the in place operand against
sibling consumer operands, the producer, and producer operands by raw pointer.
When a `dynamic-update-slice` updated `bitcast(x)` and its producer read `x`,
or the reverse, fusion added a second parameter for the same buffer. Alias
analysis then rejected in place sharing, so `CopyInsertion` inserted full
buffer copies.

Resolve operands in `xla/hlo/transforms/instruction_fusion.cc` through
`bitcast`, `tuple`, and `get-tuple-element` chains while honoring tuple shape
indices. Forbid producers that introduce a second aliasing parameter or slice a
bitcast view with a different base buffer or rank. Also peel root wrappers and
output tuples when fusing into the in place operand itself. Fusions where the
slice and update share the exact same operand, shape, and start indices remain
allowed.

Computations that previously fused reads across a bitcast into an in place
update now keep the read separate and avoid buffer copies.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:instruction_fusion_test` pins bitcast and tuple alias
  rejection, loop copy elimination, rank mismatch handling, and matching slice
  fusion.
PiperOrigin-RevId: 1026399002

display_title: [XLA] Hoist loop invariant layout changing copies in LICM

head_commit.message:
[XLA] Hoist loop invariant layout changing copies in LICM

When `WhileLoopInvariantCodeMotion` runs after layout assignment and fusion
with `hoist_reshapes` enabled and `hoist_other` disabled, it skips every opcode
other than `kConstant` and `kReshape`. That leaves unfused layout changing
`kCopy` instructions and decomposed `kBitcast` to `kCopy` or `kReshape` chains
executing inside the loop body on every iteration.

Allow `WhileLoopInvariantCodeMotion` to hoist layout changing array `kCopy`
instructions in the default memory space under `hoist_reshapes`. Also trace
through default memory space `kBitcast` operands that feed a hoisted copy or
reshape. Same layout buffer isolation copies and copies or bitcasts in any
nondefault memory space are never hoisted. Standalone bitcasts without a
hoisted user remain in the loop body and add no tuple state. The size inflation
check evaluates in double precision over layout aware shape sizes and rejects
copies that expand padded storage.

Tests:
- `//xla/hlo/transforms:while_loop_invariant_code_motion_test` pins layout copy
  and bitcast chain hoisting, attribute preservation, `CopyInsertion`, same
  layout and nondefault memory space rejection, and size inflation limits.

name: CI ROCm
display_title: Fix 32-bit overflow in SPMD pad-with-wrap rotation amount

head_commit.message:
Fix 32-bit overflow in SPMD pad-with-wrap rotation amount

In `SpmdPartitioner::PreprocessHlos` (`xla/service/spmd/spmd_partitioner.cc`),
widen `rotate_lhs_amount` from `int` to `int64_t` (matching `rotate_rhs_amount`
and `CreateCustomCallSPMDInternal_RotateRight`) so pad-with-wrap patterns with
rotation amounts exceeding `INT32_MAX` do not truncate or overflow. Also guard
the `padded_size > INT32_MAX` pad-with-wrap rewrite on matching even shardings
for `mid` and `hlo` and bounded halo size (`low_pad + high_pad <=
min(INT32_MAX, shard_size)`) so uneven sharding or large halos fall back to
standard `kConcatenate` partitioning instead of hitting 32-bit halo helpers.
